articles.title: Two held over death of cheetah; firearm as yet untraced
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Two people have been arrested in connection with the killing of a male cheetah cub at the Kuno National Park, officials said on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A senior wildlife official told The Hindu that two people had been arrested after questioning. “The arrest has been made by a special task force formed for the purpose under the Arms Act, after which the accused were produced before a court. They are currently in police remand, and we will take custody soon,” the official said, requesting anonymity.

“The case will be solved very soon, and we will reveal everything in a day or two. At the moment, multiple teams are at work,” the official said adding that more than five forest personnel had been suspended.

Another senior wildlife official, however, said that the two persons had been detained on Thursday (October 29) evening while the weapon, believed to be a country-made bharmar gun, is yet to be recovered.

“Several people in villages near the spot where the cub was found have been questioned so far and based on that two locals were detained last night [Thursday]. They were arrested today. Searches have also been conducted in the area to find the gun,” the official said, adding that the accused were being questioned about the circumstances of the incident and the firearm used.
Earlier on Thursday (October 29), officials had said that investigating teams have been scanning a large area, mapping the cub’s movement over 15-20 days based on its tracking radio-collar.
The probe is being led by a four-member special task force formed by the State Government along with the State Tiger Strike Force

Officials suspect that the weapon used in the shooting is “a country-made bharmar gun”, a traditional single-shot, muzzle-loading smoothbore firearm that is popular is the rural and forest parts of the region.

The 19-month-old cub, KNG22, an offspring of South African cheetah Nirva, had been found with five gunshot injuries in Sheopur forest division on October 25 and died during treatment on October 27 in Jabalpur. This was the first instance of a cheetah being shot since Project Cheetah, a reintroduction programme for the species, was launched in September, 2022.

fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.keyPoints:
• While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely
• Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.
• However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: U.P. CM prioritised his home turf over 2 Varanasi seats in MLC polls: Akhilesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As per the final tally, declared on Thursday afternoon, of the 11 U.P. Legislative Council seats that went to the polls on October 23, the BJP won six while the SP raised its tally from the previous MLC polls by two

Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Friday accused Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath of securing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s victory in the Gorakhpur-Faizabad division Legislative teachers’ constituency at the cost of the two Legislative Council seats in the Varanasi region. “Let Kashi drown, but our Gorakhpur business must not stop,” the senior Opposition leader remarked.

Mr. Adityanath has been a five-term MP from Gorakhpur and currently represents the Gorakhpur (Urban) constituency in the Assembly. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is currently in his third term as the Lok Sabha member from Varanasi.

As per the final tally, declared on Thursday afternoon, of the 11 U.P. Legislative Council seats that went to the polls on October 23, the BJP won six while the SP raised its tally from the previous MLC polls by two.

Addressing a media briefing at the party headquarters after meeting the party candidates, including the five winners, the SP chief said Mr. Adityanath was busy “prioritising and protecting his home turf” over his party’s prospects elsewhere. Citing the geographical spread of 11 constituencies, the former CM said the BJP had lost in 50 districts and cities.

“Legislative Council election results are just the beginning. BJP’s performance has turned out to be a flop show despite the way they misused power to win the elections. It has sent a message to the public. The BJP bagged six seats through deceit while the Samajwadi Party won on a public mandate. The BJP has financial muscle while we are competing against it through the power of the masses,” he said.

Claiming that women had voted against ruling party candidates in large numbers, Mr. Yadav said that the election results will strengthen democracy and his party’s movement “to establish the rule of social justice” and ensure justice for the PDA, which stands for ‘Pichhde’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘Alpsankhyak’ (minorities), communities.

The SP chief also hit out at the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance government in U.P. over the state of education and unemployment. “The government is ruining the education system and examination processes. It has closed 26,000 primary schools and curbed employment avenues for teachers. More than 20 examination papers have been leaked under this government,” said Mr. Yadav.

“All women teachers voted against the BJP after seeing how the government is shutting down primary schools. Where will the daughters go to study? The issues that the Samajwadi Party has raised and the promises it has made resonate with the teachers. If a Samajwadi government is formed, primary to postgraduate education will be made free,” he said.

articles.title: Moderate rain likely in south coastal Andhra Pradesh for three days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Low-pressure area over Andaman Sea is likely to concentrate into a depression over Bay of Bengal around October 31 and move towards A.P. coast in the next two days, says IMD

A low-pressure area over the south Andaman Sea is likely to concentrate into a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal around October 31 and move west-northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast during the following two days, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said.

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre (CWC), Visakhapatnam, said the system was yet to be declared a depression, and whether it would intensify further has to be watched. The remnant of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, now a low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh, no longer affects the State, he said.

Parts of the coastal districts received heavy rain on Friday. Until 6 p.m., Nagaram in Konaseema district recorded 91.5 mm, Tanuku in West Godavari 81.2 mm, Chodavaram in Anakapalli 80.2 mm, Velangi in Kakinada 76.9 mm, and Machilipatnam in Krishna 76.7 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA). Mamidikuduru in Konaseema received 54.2 mm, and Devarapalli in Anakapalli 52.5 mm.

APSDMA Managing Director Prakhar Jain said light to moderate rain was likely at places in south coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema for three days. On Sunday and Monday, moderate rain is expected at isolated places in East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, Prakasam, and Nellore. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea.

The CWC has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Palnadu, and Bapatla districts on November 2, and in West Godavari, Eluru, and Prakasam as well on November 3. Squally weather is likely along and off the coast from November 1, with winds reaching 55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, on November 2.

Maximum temperatures recorded on Friday were above normal in Rayalaseema and along the southern coast. Anantapur recorded the highest maximum of 37°C, followed by Nellore at 36.7°C, Visakhapatnam at 29.6°C, and Amaravati at 34.5°C.

An inter-ministerial Central team led by Chittaranjan Dash, Joint Secretary, Union Home Ministry, will assess the damage done by Cyclone Arnab in Konaseema, East Godavari, Kakinada, and West Godavari on Saturday and Sunday, Mr. Jain said.

Another team led by Chinmay Gotmare, Joint Secretary, Union Agriculture Ministry, will review kharif drought conditions in Sri Sathya Sai, Anantapur, Kurnool, and Nandyal on Monday and Tuesday. The State has declared 283 mandals as severely drought-affected and 105 as moderately drought-affected.
The teams are likely to meet Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday and Wednesday, respectively.

ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

fullParagraphs: In total, 7,75,803 voters to exercise their franchise in Guntur and Tenali; votes to be counted at Acharya Nagarjuna University for Guntur and VSR College for Tenali on November 3

All arrangements have been made for the elections to Guntur Municipal Corporation and Tenali Municipality scheduled for November 1, District Collector C.M. Saikanth Varma said on Friday, appealing to voters to exercise their franchise freely and fearlessly.

Addressing the media, the Collector said 596 polling stations had been set up in Guntur, with 4,514 polling personnel, while Tenali would have 185 polling stations staffed by 1,185 personnel. The polling materials would be distributed on October 31.
Elections would be held for 127 of the 128 wards, as one ward in Tenali had been unanimously elected. Guntur has 6,18,714 voters and Tenali 1,57,089, taking the combined electorate to 7,75,803.
Counting of votes would take place at Acharya Nagarjuna University for Guntur and VSR College for Tenali on November 3.

Around 1,200 police personnel would be deployed to ensure peaceful polling. Web cameras would monitor polling in sensitive and highly sensitive polling stations, while flying squads and surveillance teams would oversee election-related activities.

Meanwhile, MPTC and ZPTC elections have been rescheduled to November 5, with counting on November 7. The district has 200 MPTC and 13 ZPTC seats. Seven MPTC seats have been elected unanimously. Postal ballot facilitation centres would function across all mandals on October 30 and 31 for election personnel, the Collector said.

articles.title: NVS-03 satellite launch successful: ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System series

The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO.
The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit.

“The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said.
He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected.

The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series or the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC).
According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to spend ₹3,000 crore on irrigation drain modernisation in Godavari region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Modernisation of irrigation drains will offer a permanent solution to crop inundation problems, says Chief Minister, adding that 4.68 TMC of rainwater has been diverted to reservoirs during Cyclone Arnab

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Friday said that an estimated ₹3,000 crore would be sanctioned for the modernisation of irrigation drains, guaranteeing a permanent solution to the inundation of agricultural and horticultural fields in the Godavari region.
The backwaters are inundating standing crops and freshwater aquaculture ponds because irrigation drains are choked at their confluences.

Addressing the media after inspecting areas hit by Cyclone Arnab in Metturevu, Mogalthuru mandal, West Godavari district, Mr Naidu said the Water Resources Department had completed a survey and proposed an estimated expenditure of ₹3,000 crore to modernise irrigation drains in the Godavari region.
“We aim to guarantee a permanent solution to the inundation of crops, and it can be achieved through modernisation of drains”, Mr. Naidu said.

Referring to cyclone relief operations, Mr. Naidu assured that power restoration work for domestic connections will be completed by Sunday. He sought four more days to resume power supply for agricultural purposes.

Mr. Naidu announced ₹5 lakh ex gratia to the families of those who died during the cyclone and ₹25,000 input subsidy per hectare for damaged crops, including paddy, sugarcane, commercial and horticulture crops. This is apart from the crop insurance entitlement. He announced ₹18,000 per hectare of aquaculture ponds for loss, ₹10,000 per damaged house and ₹25,000 for handloom equipment.
Mr. Naidu said the Coconut Board would be roped in to revive the damaged coconut trees. In West Godavari district alone, 12,500 trees, mostly coconut trees, collapsed.

“Compensation ranging from ₹9,000 to ₹25,000 will be given for damaged boats based on the loss of nets,” Mr. Naidu said. More than 300 fishing boats have been damaged in the Godavari region as per the preliminary reports.

“Simultaneously, we have managed to fill the ponds and reservoirs with rainwater during the cyclone to tackle the drought conditions across the State and the water will also be used for rabi crops,” he said.
A whopping 4.68 TMC of rainwater has been diverted to reservoirs, while groundwater reserves have also improved by approximately 44 TMC due to continuous rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.
Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.
• Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: On JD(U) 23rd foundation day, party gives credit to Nitish for Bihar’s development
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: JD(U) State president pointed out that while the term “Bihari” had become synonymous with contempt and neglect before 2005, Nitish Kumar, through his efforts, restored honour and self-respect to Bihar and its people

Ruling Janata Dal (United) on Friday (October 30, 2026) celebrated its 23rd foundation day of the party and credited the party’s President and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar leadership for the Bihar’s development.

JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha wrote a message on social media account X asserting that with the trust of the people, the dedication of its workers, and the resolve for good governance, the JD(U) has carved out a distinct identity in Bihar’s politics.

“Under the leadership and guidance of our esteemed national president, Nitish Kumar ji, the party has played a pivotal role in advancing Bihar’s development, social justice, good governance, and inclusive growth. On this special occasion, heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all senior leaders, dedicated workers, and supporters of the party,”Mr. Jha wrote.
He added that we should come together to strengthen the resolve for public service and continue working tirelessly for Bihar’s progress and prosperity.

JD(U) State president Umesh Singh Kushwaha also extended greetings on the party’s foundation Day and said that the 23-year glorious journey of the JD(U) under the leadership of Nitish Kumar is dedicated to the values ​​of social justice and good governance.

Speaking to the media, he called Mr. Kumar as the party’s undisputed leader and his son Nishant Kumar who is also the Health Minister of Bihar as future leader of the party. Mr. Kushwaha said that the JD(U) was founded on October 30, 2003, drawing inspiration from the ideals of the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, Dr. Baba Saheb Bhimrao Ambedkar, Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan and Jannayak Karpoori Thakur.

“Since its inception, the party has remained committed to advancing the principles of social justice, good governance, and social harmony throughout its 23-year journey. When Nitish Kumar took the reins of Bihar in November 2005, he ushered a new era for the state,” Mr. Kushwaha said.

He added that Mr. Kumar introduced a transformative model centred on “development with justice,” good governance, and women’s empowerment that fundamentally altered both the destiny and the image of Bihar.

JD(U) State president pointed out that while the term “Bihari” had become synonymous with contempt and neglect before 2005, Nitish Kumar, through his efforts, restored honour and self-respect to Bihar and its people.
In his congratulatory message, Mr. Kushwaha asked all the party workers and leaders to take a resolve to move the JD(U) to unprecedented heights of success in days to come.

articles.title: Deeply distressing to see ambulances stranded, students missing classes during convoy movement in Kashmir: Sakina Itoo
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sakina Ittoo appealed to L-G Sinha “to explore practical traffic management measures that uphold essential security protocols while ensuring uninterrupted passage for ambulances and minimising public inconvenience.”

J&K Cabinet minister Sakina Itoo on Friday (October 30, 2026) sought intervention of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha to end stringent drills during the movement of security forces’ convoys in Kashmir.

Ms. Itoo, who represents a constituency in south Kashmir’s Kulgam, in a post on X, highlighted the inconvenience faced by locals during the movement of security forces. After the Pulwama attack, security forces stop traffic on both tubes of the highway till convoys move.

“While travelling frequently on the Srinagar–Anantnag–Kulgam–Qazigund National Highway, it is deeply distressing to see ambulances stranded, students missing classes and ordinary citizens waiting 15–30 minutes, sometimes even hours, for convoy movement. What fault have our people committed to endure such hardships?” said Ms. Itoo.

She appealed to L-G Sinha and the concerned authorities “to explore practical traffic management measures that uphold essential security protocols while ensuring uninterrupted passage for ambulances and minimising public inconvenience.”

“Security is paramount, but so is the well-being of our people. Security and compassion must go hand in hand. Let governance be reflected not just in policies, but in the everyday lives of citizens through dignity, sensitivity and meaningful relief,” said Ms. Itoo.

J&K Cabinet minister Sakina Itoo on Friday (October 30, 2026) sought intervention of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha to end stringent drills during the movement of security forces’ convoys in Kashmir.

Ms. Itoo, who represents a constituency in south Kashmir’s Kulgam, in a post on X, highlighted the inconvenience faced by locals during the movement of security forces. After the Pulwama attack, security forces stop traffic on both tubes of the highway till convoys move.

“While travelling frequently on the Srinagar–Anantnag–Kulgam–Qazigund National Highway, it is deeply distressing to see ambulances stranded, students missing classes and ordinary citizens waiting 15–30 minutes, sometimes even hours, for convoy movement. articles.title: 17 NC MLAs issue 15-day ultimatum to address ‘coterie culture’, other issues in party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four-hour meeting of the 17 NC legislators in Srinagar comes three days after party vice-president and J&K CM Omar Abdullah expanded the Cabinet, leaving several leaders disgruntled at not being given a berth

At least 17 legislators from the ruling National Conference (NC) on Friday (October 30, 2026) held a four-hour meeting in Srinagar and issued a 15-day ultimatum to party president Farooq Abdullah and vice-president Omar Abdullah to address issues, including “unilateral decisions” and “coterie culture”.

The meeting, which started around 3 p.m. and ended at 6 p.m., was held at the residence of NC legislator Qaiser Jamsheed Lone in Srinagar’s Friends Colony. Senior NC leaders, including Mubarak Gul, Nazir Gurezi, and Abdul Majeed Larmi, were among those in attendance. An Independent legislator, Muzaffar Iqbal Khan from the Thanamandi constituency, also attended.

The rebellion within the party came three days after party vice-president and Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expanded the Cabinet, increasing the number of ministers from six to nine. Since then, many legislators have publicly expressed their anger and demanded their inclusion. They included Mr. Gul, Mr. Gurezi and Mr. Larmi. Around a dozen NC legislators boycotted a dinner hosted by party president Farooq Abdullah after the Cabinet expansion.

An NC legislator, who attended the meeting, told The Hindu that a joint resolution was passed at the meeting and that it would be shared with the party leadership with a 15-day ultimatum to address the issues.

“A kitchen cabinet system and the coterie culture have to end. Such a culture is dominating the functioning of the party right now. There was no formal or informal consultation with the elected leaders ahead of the Cabinet expansion. This is an unhealthy party culture. It is a rebellion in favour of the party,” said the NC leader.
Another NC leader accused Omar Abdullah’s adviser Nasir Aslam Wani and MP Shami Oberoi of “insulating Mr. Abdullah and imposing decisions on elected members”.

“The party has to respect its own MLAs. People voted the NC to power with certain expectations. The party should discuss its failures of the past two years and work on its manifesto,” said another NC legislator.
The legislators were also unhappy with the Chief Minister’s “unfair distribution of portfolios despite the complaints raised against Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary”.

“There has been no application of mind in distributing the portfolios. The party should take MLAs on board and take decisions in a democratic fashion. Those who failed to perform as ministers in the past two years should be dropped and not rewarded with key portfolios,” said an MLA.
Another legislator said it was not about portfolios or ministries but the “party’s functioning”. “Dr. [Farooq] Abdullah has to address the issues faced by the party,” the MLA added.

articles.title: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation; satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks

The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO.
The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit.

“The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said.
He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected.

The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series or the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC).
According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks.
“It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said.

NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area.

The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.
It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working.

“It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said.

NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area.

The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.

It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working.

articles.title: Failed relationships cannot turn consensual sex into rape: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court distinguishes between consent allegedly obtained through deception and regret over consensual intimacy after a relationship ends
The Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) held that women cannot convert consensual sexual acts into rape after the relationship turns sour.

“We wish to note a worrying trend in recent years wherein consensual relationships that have come to an end are retrospectively combed with a fine tooth so as to identify what can post-facto be construed as violence and sexual assault,” Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed in a judgment.

The verdict came in a case from Kerala in which a man was accused of repeated instances of rape during a seven-year relationship which didn’t work out. The complainant had said that she was kept in the dark about the fact that he was already married and a father to two children from the previous marriage.

Justice Nagarathna said a clear distinguishing line must be drawn between an absence of consent because it was got by deception, and the experience of regret over having consented to past sexual acts after the relationship ends.

“While the latter scenario is unfortunate, such hindsight on its own cannot constitute a consensual relationship as a crime… In fact, such an approach denudes the man of any agency entirely, as the mere factum of being in a consensual relationship at one point would bind him to it entirely for fear of being accused of rape at a subsequent point of time,” the court observed.
Physical intimacy that occurred during a relationship cannot be retrospectively branded as acts of rape merely because the relationship soured and no longer subsists, the court concluded.

“This court has time and again witnessed the disturbing trend where failed relationships are being converted into criminal cases. Rape, being a heinous offence, must be reserved for situations where there is real sexual violence, coercion, or manipulation of consent. When every consensual relationship which sours is converted into an accusation of rape, it not only dilutes the gravity of the offence alleged, it also subjects the accused to irreparable stigma, harassment and injustice,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out in the judgment.
However, the court also sounded a note of caution, saying rape was one of the most under-reported crimes and struck at the core of a woman’s bodily autonomy and dignity.

“For every case where the provisions related to rape are misused, there are several cases that never see the light of day. We must emphasise that genuine cases must be pursued with vigour where the facts clearly show sexual assault and violence. But equally, the justice system must not be turned into a tool of vengeance when relationships fail,” Justice Nagarathna observed.

articles.title: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood damages roads, washes away bridge in Bhutan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Vulnerable revenue circles in Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts of Assam have been put on high alert

GELEPHU (BHUTAN) A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Shintapu Tsho in the Laya area of northwestern Bhutan’s Gasa district on Thursday night (October 29, 2026) triggered flooding along the Mochhu, damaging roads, bridges and public infrastructure in two districts.

Officials on Friday (October 30, 2026) said no human casualties have been reported, but there are growing concerns over a large artificial lake formed near Taktsemakhang, about 2,000 feet downstream of Laya. The accumulation of water at the confluence of the flood-affected channels of Mochhu (river) has raised fears of another sudden outburst, which could be disastrous for downstream areas.

Officials said they could not immediately assess the GLOF impact on Thursday night (October 29, 2026). Royal Bhutan Army personnel stationed at Taktsemakhang and people near Gasa Tshachu, a hot spring, were instructed to evacuate to a safer location.

“Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay is in Laya to assess the artificial lake at Taktesakhang, while Industry, Commerce and Employment Minister Namgyel Dorji is monitoring the situation in Punakha,” a Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management official said.

Punakha and Thimphu districts are south of Gasa, which borders the Tibetan Autonomous Region. These and other neighbouring districts were put on high alert for potential danger from the GLOF-induced artificial lake.

According to disaster management officials, Gasa Tsachu, one of Bhutan’s popular hot spring destinations, suffered extensive damage due to Thursday’s (October 29, 2026) GLOF. Floodwaters washed away almost all public facilities in the area.
This was the second flood-related damage at Gasa Tshachu since August 26, 2021, when the swollen Mochhu changed course towards the area.
The GLOF also damaged two vital roads in Gasa district and swept away a Bailey bridge in Punakha district. The bridge was constructed in 2022 with support from the Government of India.

In Assam, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the State government was closely monitoring the possible impact of the Bhutan GLOF. “The vulnerable revenue circles in (western Assam’s) Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts have been put on high alert,” he said.

Shintaphu Tsho (Lake), located at the source of the Mochhu, is among Bhutan’s 17 glacial lakes identified as potentially dangerous. The Mochhu, considered female, and Phochhu (male) meet in Punakha district to form the Punatsangchhu, which flows along the Assam-West Bengal border as the Sonkosh River.

fullParagraphs: Police said they detained three people after some protesters breached the tribunal's fence and others threw objects at officers

Police secured Poland's Constitutional Tribunal as dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they perceive as the wrongful suspension of the top court's president by the current pro-European government.
Police said they detained three people after some protesters breached the tribunal's fence and others threw objects at officers.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki, who was flying to Senegal, said he turned his flight back because of the situation. “At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland. I am cutting short my flight to Senegal. I am returning,” he wrote on X.

Poland's top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS).

Critics in Poland and the European Union accuse PiS, which led the country between 2015 and 2023, of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, including the Constitutional Tribunal. The PiS reforms led the EU to impose fines on Poland.

The pro-European government of Donald Tusk came to power in 2023 with a promise to restore the independence of the judiciary. Since then, the government's efforts have been blocked by vetoes from two successive presidents aligned with PiS, including Nawrocki.

The information about the suspension of the president of the Constitutional Tribunal, Bogdan Swieczkowski, was published on the website of the court around 6 p.m. local time. The website of the Tribunal went down soon after, so The Associated Pres s could not independently verify the official reasons given for his suspension.

Mr. Swieczkowski became head of the Constitutional Tribunal under the PiS government, and Mr. Tusk has accused him of blocking judges elected by the parliamentary majority from taking up their posts at the tribunal.

“Restoring the rule of law is our obligation," Prime Minister Tusk wrote on X on Friday evening (October 30, 2026). "After years of lawlessness under PiS, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.”

The Kadavanthra police have registered a case against a premium hotel in Kochi city on charges of hosting a DJ party and selling liquor at its bar beyond the permissible hours, in violation of licence conditions.

The case was registered against Radisson Blu Hotel in Elamkulam following a search operation in the early hours of Saturday (October 31, 2026). It has been booked under Sections 55(h) of the Kerala Abkari Act (whoever prints, publishes, or gives any advertisement soliciting the use of, or offering, any liquor or intoxicating drug) and 56(b) (wilfully doing or omitting to do anything in breach of the conditions of a licence or permit).

According to the FIR, the DJ party was held after advertisements encouraging alcohol consumption. The police seized electronic equipment used for the party along with documents. The search, which began around 2 a.m., lasted for over an hour.
Customers present at the bar during the operation were reportedly let off after being examined.

articles.title: INDIA bloc to hold ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Friday (October 30) said he would participate in the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally in Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and the demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
“We will go [to Delhi] on November 1. We will also participate in the rally,” Mr. Yadav said at a presser.

Segueing into his sarcastic style, Mr. Yadav also called for “better-quality” photographs on voter ID cards, saying the pictures in electoral rolls were often so unclear that one could not recognise a person.

Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav has constituted 20 committees to oversee arrangements for the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan, with responsibilities ranging from accommodation to venue management, sanitation and social media.

According to an official statement, the committees were approved by Yadav to coordinate various aspects of the rally, which is being organised by the opposition alliance to protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

A major rally led by the Congress and attended by the Left parties and other INDIA bloc members scheduled at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on November 1, as part of a countrywide protest against the EC will be “huge,” CPI General Secretary D Raja said on Friday (October 30).

Addressing the media, Mr. Raja stated that the INDIA bloc is again spearheading a nationwide campaign demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid public anger over the SIR.

The CPI leader asserted that the Election Commission must function as an impartial and neutral body to ensure free and fair elections and protect the people’s right to vote. He further demanded that the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls be withdrawn.

The BJP on Friday (October 30) rejected as a “lie” Rahul Gandhi’s claim that Home Minister Amit Shah is trying to stop people from coming to Delhi for the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally in Delhi and asked the Congress leader to stop misleading people by spreading falsehood.
Addressing a press conference, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also demanded that Mr. Gandhi show proof of his allegation.

articles.title: Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi denies defending SIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Satish Jarkiholi, minister and Congress leader, has clarified that he never defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka. He claimed his remarks were misquoted and taken out of context.

Following a press meet in Bengaluru on October 29, the minister was quoted as saying that he had found nothing wrong with SIR and that the Congress party had raised objections to the exercise in other States but not in Karnataka.
The Minister issued a statement on October 30, saying his remarks were misunderstood.

“While responding to questions from the media, I had said that under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and the guidance of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, measures have been taken to prevent such attempts, that were allegedly orchestrated by the BJP, to delete names of eligible voters. I had only said that the objections raised by Congress leaders against the misuse of Form 7 were addressed by the authorities. The issue was concerning the alleged misuse in Belagavi district, and a police case was registered in connection with it. The media has also reported the police investigation into the issue,” he said.

“We have discovered that around 17,000 – 25,000 votes were deleted from the electoral roll in the Yamakanamardi Assembly constituency that I represent. Our team is conducting a comprehensive review of the new electoral rolls. We are also waiting for the final electoral list of all constituencies that will be prepared following court judgments, and changes to some rules. We are concerned about the deletion of names of migrant workers and young students who have moved to other cities for studies. If their names are missing from one place, they should reflect in other places. All such issues need to be fixed,” he said.

articles.title: West Asia crisis triggers payment concern in Keralam’s cardamom sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cardamom growers voice serious concern over extended delays in receiving payments from auctioneers. Usually, auction houses clear dues to planters within 15 days; currently, disbursements take over a month
The ongoing West Asia crisis has disrupted payments to cardamom exporters from Gulf countries, triggering liquidity concerns and widespread uncertainty across the sector.

​Cardamom growers have voiced serious concern over extended delays in receiving payments from auctioneers. Usually, auction houses cleared dues to planters within 15 days; currently, disbursements take over a month.
​Exporters attribute the cash crunch directly to geopolitical tensions in West Asia .

​”Earlier, shipments to Gulf nations were settled within seven days. Now, it take between 60 and 70 days because consignments face unexpected shipping and clearance delays,” said Santhosh Allus, a cardamom exporter based in Kumily. “This is an industry worth roughly ₹4,500 crore, and a choke in cash flow has a cascading effect on every stakeholder.”

​Mr. Allus added that while many growers recognise the prevailing export crisis and are cooperating with auctioneers, rigid payment enforcement risks backfiring. “If growers insist on immediate settlement, only buyers with deep liquidity can participate in the auctions. That would compel auctioneers to turn down lots or restrict trade, inevitably triggering a price collapse,” he explained.
​Compounding the problem is this season’s sharp surge in cardamom prices, said Joshy Joseph, public relations officer of Spice More Group, an auction firm licensed by the Spices Board.

​”When prices were lower, three or four major groups comfortably used to procure substantial volumes,” said Mr. Joseph. “With minimum average prices now surpassing ₹3,000 per kilogram, purchasing requires significantly higher working capital. Numerous smaller merchant groups have entered the bidding ring, which slows down the collection cycle,” said Mr Joseph.
​Spices Board chairperson Sangeetha Viswanathan confirmed that the board has received a grievance from a planter regarding unpaid auction dues.

​”I have sought an urgent report from the Spices Board field offices in Puttady (Idukki) and Bodinayakanur (Tamil Nadu). Officials have been directed to submit their findings within two days. Once the reports are in hand, we will initiate necessary action,” Ms. Viswanathan said on Thursday, adding that the board will also conduct sensitisation drives among auctioneers to safeguard timely settlements for growers.
​Trade sources noted that banking and market closures in north India during the Pooja and Deepavali festival seasons have further contributed to temporary liquidity constraints.

articles.title: North Korean hackers linked to crypto thefts among world's best, experts say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A US State Department ‌spokesman said North Korean cybercrime is a “global problem”

North Korean hackers likely behind the record $6.3 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Binance are among the world’s most prolific crypto thieves, and the proceeds help fund ​the country’s weapons programs, cybersecurity experts said on Friday.

Blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attribute the heist ‌to a North Korean hacking group known as “TraderTraitor,” a name used in ​a 2022 joint warning from the FBI, CISA and US Treasury that ⁠described how hackers used malicious software and other tricks to target software developers and IT staff at cryptocurrency companies.

North Korea stole at least $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency through the end of 2025, Chainalysis said in a ‌December 2025 report. That total includes the $1.5 billion ByBit exchange hack in February 2025.

The group also hit Bitget, a separate exchange, taking $387 million in September, experts have said, ‌bringing the minimum total of cryptocurrency North Korea has stolen to roughly $13.5 billion, said Michael ‌Barnhart, ⁠a researcher with cybersecurity firm DTEX.
Binance said it and others were working ⁠to freeze some of the stolen cryptocurrency, with about $3 billion located so far.
“After Bitget, a lot of the community expected something like this,” Barnhart said.

TraderTraitor is North Korea’s “most capable hacking group with a primary focus on financials and one ​staffed by some of the most experienced ‌operators in the regime’s cyber programs in the former APT38 ranks,” he added, referring to North Korea’s long-running financially focused hacking units.

Researchers say TraderTraitor targets developers and IT staff at financial institutions through malware or phony job offers, tricking candidates into downloading malicious software during fake ‌job interviews, giving the hackers access to login credentials and other sensitive data.

Rafe Pilling, ​a senior director of threat research at Sophos, said early reports of how the hackers compromised Binance match the North Korean playbook, and that the ⁠group is expert at working out how a company’s systems and staff approve money transfers. “This group in particular are somewhat artists in terms of getting into these distributed finance companies,” he said.
After stealing the money, the hackers pass it to Chinese organised crime money-laundering groups, Barnhart said.

North Korean hackers likely behind the record $6.3 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Binance are among the world’s most prolific crypto thieves, and the proceeds help fund ​the country’s weapons programs, cybersecurity experts said on Friday.

Blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attribute the heist ‌to a North Korean hacking group known as “TraderTraitor,” a name used in ​a 2022 joint warning from the FBI, CISA and US Treasury that ⁠described how hackers used malicious software and other tricks to target software developers and IT staff at cryptocurrency companies.

North Korea stole at least $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency through the end of 2025, Chainalysis said in a ‌December 2025 report. That total includes the $1.5 billion ByBit exchange hack in February 2025.

The group also hit Bitget, a separate exchange, taking $387 million in September, experts have said, ‌bringing the minimum total of cryptocurrency North Korea has stolen to roughly $13.5 billion, said Michael ‌Barnhart, ⁠a researcher with cybersecurity firm DTEX.

Binance said it and others were working ⁠to freeze some of the stolen cryptocurrency, with about $3 billion located so far.

“After Bitget, a lot of the community expected something like this,” Barnhart said.

TraderTraitor is North Korea’s “most capable hacking group with a primary focus on financials and one ​staffed by some of the most experienced ‌operators in the regime’s cyber programs in the former APT38 ranks,” he added, referring to North Korea’s long-running financially focused hacking units.

Researchers say TraderTraitor targets developers and IT staff at financial institutions through malware or phony job offers, tricking candidates into downloading malicious software during fake ‌job interviews, giving the hackers access to login credentials and other sensitive data.

Rafe Pilling, ​a senior director of threat research at Sophos, said early reports of how the hackers compromised Binance match the North Korean playbook, and that the ⁠group is expert at working out how a company’s systems and staff approve money transfers. “This group in particular are somewhat artists in terms of getting into these distributed finance companies,” he said.

After stealing the money, the hackers pass it to Chinese organised crime money-laundering groups, Barnhart said.

articles.title: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026)

Israel's final election results confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead.

The results released early Friday (October 30, 2026) showed Mr. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) election. The main Opposition bloc won 48. Arab-led parties secured the other 19, a historic showing. Now parties must meet, bargain and seek a way to team up for at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, remains in charge.

“Now comes the truly hard part,” centrist politician Yair Lapid said on X, urging patience and adding, “If you want to know if something's happening behind the silence you're hearing now, the answer is yes.”

Difficult decisions lie ahead. Will the main Opposition parties that campaigned hard to unseat the divisive Mr. Netanyahu make the politically sensitive choice to partner with Arab-led ones? Or will they toss their vows aside to team up with Mr. Netanyahu in a potentially fractious unity government?

Friday (October 30, 2026) is when much of Israel starts winding down for Shabbat, and it was not clear who might be meeting with whom. Israelis debated possible coalitions and challenges, as some expressed traditional wariness around Arab parties and others insisted it was time for Israel to take a deep breath and embrace them.
“There are options for all of this, not like in the United States, where there are only two parties,” said Beny Engalrd, a resident of Tel Aviv.

The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026). Then President Isaac Herzog will task someone with forming the new government. That could be the leader of the party that received the most votes — Mr. Netanyahu — or whoever the leaders of the various parties believe is best suited.
If multiple attempts to form a government fail, Israel faces a new election early next year. Mr. Herzog this week said he will do everything in his power to avoid that scenario.

In the hours before final results were announced, Mr. Netanyahu and his Likud party amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance.

articles.title: U.S., South Korea, Japan vow ‘complete’ North Korea’s denuclearisation
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Mr. Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks

The United States, South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the “complete denuclearisation” of North Korea on Saturday (October 31, 2026), as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible talks with Washington.

Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Mr. Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearisation” of North Korea during talks on Friday (October 30) on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta in the U.S. state of Georgia, the U.S. State Department said.
They also pledged “full implementation” of UN Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.
Mr. Trump has made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks, while scaling back joint military drills with ally South Korea.

The mercurial U.S. leader even bucked long-held U.S. policy last year by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”, while reaching out to Pyongyang for talks, saying he was “100%” open to a meeting — a suggestion that went unanswered.
Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Mr. Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Mr. Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.

South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief.
Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal.

articles.title: U.S. scraps G20 family photo after Europeans object to being pictured with Russia's Lavrov
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The cancellation has added to concerns about the poor prospects for the G20 diplomats to reach consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face

The U.S. scrapped plans for a photo of top diplomats of the Group of 20 largest world economies on the opening day of talks on Friday (October 30, 2026) as several Europeans objected to being photographed with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to walk out of the photo session.

The cancellation of the photograph, a traditional opening event at such a diplomatic gathering, underscored the deep rifts in the G20 over global crises that threaten international security and trade.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio decided to cancel the photo after determining that the controversy would be a distraction, according to two U.S. officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. The meeting in Atlanta, which will otherwise go ahead as planned, is meant to set the stage for a G20 leaders' summit hosted by President Donald Trump at his Miami golf club in December.

The cancellation has added to concerns about the poor prospects for the G20 diplomats to reach consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face. Among them are the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese machinations in the South China Sea. All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel as well as uncertainty about trade.

Before the photo disagreement, some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine. That is especially after Mr. Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance.

Russia's Foreign Ministry complained of issues securing visas for its delegation that were only resolved at the last minute. Those complications had created the impression that “not everyone in Washington is happy” about Mr. Lavrov attending, ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said. But he would use the meeting to advocate for the “swift reform of global economic institutions,” she said.

Mr. Lavrov has travelled very infrequently to NATO member states since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and resulting severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow. His presence in Atlanta is likely to cause domestic political problems for Mr. Trump just days before the midterm elections and roil at least the G20's Western participants, according to Ian Kelly, a U.S. ambassador to Georgia during Mr. Trump's first term.
“It seems politically boneheaded to invite him,” said Mr. Kelly, who now teaches international relations and diplomacy at Northwestern University outside Chicago.

Mr. Kelly noted that many Republican lawmakers, who already fear losing their congressional majorities, are “cranky” with Mr. Trump's conciliatory approach to Mr. Putin. Democrats, he added, could use the invitation to bash the GOP before the midterm Election Day on Tuesday (November 3).

In terms of the G20 itself, Mr. Lavrov's attendance will almost certainly hurt efforts to produce a unified approach on the Russia-Ukraine war, Mr. Kelly said. “It will definitely take away from the message that at least the Western members want to send,” he said.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: "The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," Mr. Bolsonaro said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation
Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday (October 30, 2026) that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's (October 25) election runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday (October 27) and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday (October 28) after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador.

"The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation.
In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.
"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.
Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone."
U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape.
"I didn't leave Brazil; I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him.
He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been.

articles.title: U.S. imprisons two Chinese nationals for spying
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Department of Justice said the men had carried out clandestine intelligence activities in the United States that included facilitating "dead drop" cash payments in exchange for information related to the national security of the United States
Two Chinese men who admitted trying to recruit U.S. military service members to spy for Beijing were imprisoned in California on Friday (October 30, 2026).

Liren Lai and Yuance Chen were ordered to serve 30 months in a federal lockup and to undergo three years of supervised release after pleading guilty to acting on the orders of China's Ministry of State Security.

The U.S. Department of Justice said the men had carried out clandestine intelligence activities in the United States that included facilitating "dead drop" cash payments in exchange for information related to the national security of the United States.
They also gathered information on U.S. military personnel and installations and attempted to recruit intelligence assets within the U.S. military.

"Let this sentencing serve as a clear warning: If you attempt to jeopardise the safety and security of our service members, our citizens, or our nation, justice will find you," said Roman Rozhavsky, assistant director of the FBI's Counterintelligence and Espionage Division.

Lai, who arrived in the U.S. on a tourist visa, recruited Chen — a permanent resident — into the scheme and initially served as an intermediary between Chen and intelligence officers, until Chen was able to receive his orders directly from his handler.
The DoJ said the two men had been working since at least May 2021 for the branch of the Chinese government responsible for conducting foreign intelligence and counterintelligence operations.

They were arrested in June 2025. Both men pleaded guilty to conspiracy to act as agents of a foreign government without prior notification to the Attorney General and acting as agents of a foreign government without prior notification over the following months.

articles.title: NVS-03 launched successfully; satellite placed in intended orbit | Highlights
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NVS-03 satellite is equipped with an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks

The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal
ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

Sriharikota [Andhra Pradesh], Oct 29 (ANI): A view of the NVS-03 satellite, which will enter the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit in the 20th GSLV-F18 flight from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Thursday. The launch is scheduled for October 30. (@isro X/ANI Photo)

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.
