articles.title: Cyclone Arnab highlights: Relief air-dropped in Odisha’s Ganjam; new system may turn into depression by October 31
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Power to homes in Andhra Pradesh’s cyclone-hit areas will be restored by Sunday, says Naidu

Power supply to homes in cyclone-hit areas will be restored by Sunday (November 1, 2026), Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said after visiting Mogalthuru mandal in West Godavari district on Friday.

Farm connections will take four more days, he said. Crops on more than 3.5 lakh hectares have been submerged across the State. About 2,425 km of State roads have been damaged, according to the government. In West Godavari alone, about 12,500 trees, most of them coconut, were uprooted.- T. Appala Naidu

Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi surveyed the flood-hit areas of Ganjam and Gajapati districts from the air on Friday, along with Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari. He asked officials to speed up relief and rescue work, repair damaged roads and bridges, restore power and guard against disease once the water recedes.

Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai has asked district Collectors to survey crops damaged by Cyclone Arnab and make sure farmers are compensated on time, officials said on Friday. Videos from several districts show paddy flattened by three days of wind and rain.
State Congress president Deepak Baij alleged that no survey had begun yet. He demanded a one-time compensation of ₹70,518 an acre for farmers whose crops were wiped out.

The low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea moved west-northwest overnight and lay over the south Andaman Sea and the nearby Andaman and Nicobar Islands on Friday morning, the IMD said in an X post. It is expected to become a depression around Saturday (October 31). It will then move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following two days.

South Central Railway has rescheduled four more trains on Friday because of the flooding on the line near Ichchapuram. The Howrah-Secunderabad Falaknuma Express will leave at 2.45 p.m. instead of 8.25 a.m. The Bhubaneswar-Secunderabad Visakha Express will leave at 10.30 a.m. instead of 8 a.m. The CSMT Mumbai-Bhubaneswar Express has been cancelled on October 31.
The Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Vande Bharat Express is among 35 trains cancelled after water rose over railway bridges near Ichchapuram following Cyclone Arnab.

About 10,000 people from Ichchapuram and nearby villages in Srikakulam district have been moved to relief camps in schools after the Bahuda flooded the area. Many others are still in their flooded homes where the strong current has made rescue hard. Vehicles are yet to be allowed on the Kolkata-Chennai national highway near the town, and power is still out across the Ichchapuram constituency. The water is receding fast, Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar said.
About 10,000 people are in relief camps in flood-hit Ichchapuram after the Bahuda swelled; crops on 21,519 hectares are damaged in Srikakulam, initial estimates show.

Power to homes in Andhra Pradesh’s cyclone-hit areas will be restored by Sunday, says Naidu

Power supply to homes in cyclone-hit areas will be restored by Sunday (November 1, 2026), Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said after visiting Mogalthuru mandal in West Godavari district on Friday.

Farm connections will take four more days, he said. Crops on more than 3.5 lakh hectares have been submerged across the State. About 2,425 km of State roads have been damaged, according to the government. In West Godavari alone, about 12,500 trees, most of them coconut, were uprooted.- T. Appala Naidu

Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi surveyed the flood-hit areas of Ganjam and Gajapati districts from the air on Friday, along with Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari. He asked officials to speed up relief and rescue work, repair damaged roads and bridges, restore power and guard against disease once the water recedes.

Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai has asked district Collectors to survey crops damaged by Cyclone Arnab and make sure farmers are compensated on time, officials said on Friday. Videos from several districts show paddy flattened by three days of wind and rain.

State Congress president Deepak Baij alleged that no survey had begun yet. He demanded a one-time compensation of ₹70,518 an acre for farmers whose crops were wiped out.

The low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea moved west-northwest overnight and lay over the south Andaman Sea and the nearby Andaman and Nicobar Islands on Friday morning, the IMD said in an X post. It is expected to become a depression around Saturday (October 31). It will then move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following two days.

South Central Railway has rescheduled four more trains on Friday because of the flooding on the line near Ichchapuram. The Howrah-Secunderabad Falaknuma Express will leave at 2.45 p.m. instead of 8.25 a.m. The Bhubaneswar-Secunderabad Visakha Express will leave at 10.30 a.m. instead of 8 a.m. The CSMT Mumbai-Bhubaneswar Express has been cancelled on October 31.

The Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Vande Bharat Express is among 35 trains cancelled after water rose over railway bridges near Ichchapuram following Cyclone Arnab.

About 10,000 people from Ichchapuram and nearby villages in Srikakulam district have been moved to relief camps in schools after the Bahuda flooded the area. Many others are still in their flooded homes where the strong current has made rescue hard. Vehicles are yet to be allowed on the Kolkata-Chennai national highway near the town, and power is still out across the Ichchapuram constituency. The water is receding fast, Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar said.

About 10,000 people are in relief camps in flood-hit Ichchapuram after the Bahuda swelled; crops on 21,519 hectares are damaged in Srikakulam, initial estimates show.

articles.title: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026)

Israel's final election results confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead.

The results released early Friday (October 30, 2026) showed Mr. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) election. The main Opposition bloc won 48. Arab-led parties secured the other 19, a historic showing. Now parties must meet, bargain and seek a way to team up for at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, remains in charge.

“Now comes the truly hard part,” centrist politician Yair Lapid said on X, urging patience and adding, “If you want to know if something's happening behind the silence you're hearing now, the answer is yes.”

Difficult decisions lie ahead. Will the main Opposition parties that campaigned hard to unseat the divisive Mr. Netanyahu make the politically sensitive choice to partner with Arab-led ones? Or will they toss their vows aside to team up with Mr. Netanyahu in a potentially fractious unity government?

Friday (October 30, 2026) is when much of Israel starts winding down for Shabbat, and it was not clear who might be meeting with whom. Israelis debated possible coalitions and challenges, as some expressed traditional wariness around Arab parties and others insisted it was time for Israel to take a deep breath and embrace them.
“There are options for all of this, not like in the United States, where there are only two parties,” said Beny Engalrd, a resident of Tel Aviv.

The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026). Then President Isaac Herzog will task someone with forming the new government. That could be the leader of the party that received the most votes — Mr. Netanyahu — or whoever the leaders of the various parties believe is best suited.
If multiple attempts to form a government fail, Israel faces a new election early next year. Mr. Herzog this week said he will do everything in his power to avoid that scenario.

In the hours before final results were announced, Mr. Netanyahu and his Likud party amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance.

articles.title: Israeli forces committed war crimes, genocide even after Gaza ceasefire: UN Commission
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar said.

Israeli authorities and forces have continued to commit war crimes , crimes against humanity and genocide in the occupied Palestinian territory even after the ceasefire agreement in Gaza, a United Nations commission of inquiry has said.

In a report presented to the UN General Assembly, the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory said Israeli military operations and settler violence in the West Bank were part of a coordinated attack against Palestinians, aimed at entrenching settlements, annexing Palestinian territory and displacing its population.

The Commission, Chaired by Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, said more than 75,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,500 children and 11,000 women, had been killed across the occupied Palestinian territory since October 7, 2023, the day Hamas carried out an attack in Israel, killing 1,200 people. It said the death toll had continued to rise despite the October 2025 ceasefire.

“Failure to act now is particularly egregious against the backdrop of the staggering death toll, which has continued to rise since the so-called ceasefire,” said Justice Muralidhar in his statement at the UN on October 26.

In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, he said.
The findings contradicted claims by the Board of Peace in its May report to the Security Council that the ceasefire had largely held and brought enormous relief to civilians.

The Justice said the situation in the West Bank had deteriorated significantly since October 2023. The commission concluded that Israel had committed crimes against humanity, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence. It also accused Israeli authorities of persecution through discriminatory rules of engagement that applied exclusively to Palestinians.

The report traced the roots of Israeli violence to policies dating back to the 1947-48 war, arguing that Israel had sought to maximise territorial control while minimising the Palestinian population through displacement and the use of lethal force.

The report also documents the expansion of Israeli military operations in the West Bank, including air strikes and the destruction of refugee camps. It says military operations since January 2025 have resulted in the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 people still displaced as of August 2026.

Justice Muralidhar, addressing the gathering via a video link, also criticised Palestinian security forces for using unnecessary or disproportionate force against Palestinians in the West Bank. It said the Palestinian Authority had failed to conduct effective and impartial investigations into killings and provide remedies to victims.

articles.title: Drone strikes kill 14, including children, in Ethiopia's Amhara: witnesses
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The strikes at the camp occurred just as the students were coming home from school, recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses

At least 14 people, including children, were killed in several drone strikes on Thursday (October 29, 2026) on a camp for displaced people in Ethiopia's Amhara region, three witnesses told AFP on Friday (October 30).

"Four drone strikes were carried out one after another. We have buried 14 people at the IDP centre. Two more died while receiving medical treatment," said Yasin, who requested anonymity, adding that pregnant women and children were among the victims.
Two other residents of the camp, one of whom said he had buried bodies, reported 14 and 15 deaths respectively, including several children.
The strikes at the camp, 400 kilometres (250 miles) northeast of Addis Ababa, occurred "just as the students were coming home from school," recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses.
"My sister-in-law was killed, and we couldn't even find her body because it was dismembered," he said.
The NGO Acled, which specialises in collecting and analysing data on armed conflicts, said between "16 and 23 people were killed, and an unknown number of people were injured."
It did not provide details as to whether children were among the victims.

Forces from Addis Ababa have carried out numerous drone strikes in Amhara, Ethiopia's second most populous region with more than 20 million inhabitants and where nearly half a million people are displaced, according to figures published by the United Nations in July.
Questioned by AFP , the spokesperson for the Ethiopian federal army has so far not responded.
According to the witnesses, the displaced people are originally from Oromia, the region neighbouring Amhara and the most populous in the country.

The legislation prohibits AI chatbots from engaging in potentially harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships, encouraging emotional dependency, and promoting self-harm. articles.title: TRAI proposes board-approved AI policies, mandatory reporting of serious incidents by telcos
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: TRAI said it has floated the draft ‘Guidelines on Responsible Use of AI in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services’ for stakeholders' comments.

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), on Friday (October 30, 2026), proposed a comprehensive draft framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in telecom networks that would require service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, establish dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator.

The draft guidelines, released for stakeholder consultations, also seek to make entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems deployed in their networks and services, "irrespective of whether AI systems are developed internally, procured/ outsourced from a third party or a combination thereof."

A look at the consultation paper shows that under the proposed framework, telecom operators and other authorised entities using AI will have to classify their AI systems into high-, medium- and low-risk categories based on their significance to network operations, financial and operational outcomes, and potential implications for consumers.

Each entity will be required to formulate an internal AI policy, approved by its board of directors or equivalent governing body, covering risk classification, deployment approvals, incident management, human oversight, data governance and consumer grievance redressal.
"All AI systems shall be subject to an appropriate human oversight for risk mitigation as per a predefined mechanism," the consultation paper said.

The regulator has proposed that AI-related incidents be classified into four categories, namely critical, high, moderate and low severity, with critical and high-severity incidents mandatorily reported to TRAI.
"Critical severity AI incidents and high severity AI incidents shall be informed to TRAI in a prescribed format, manner and timeframe," it said.
Telecom companies will also have to maintain central databases of AI incidents and consumer complaints involving AI-related harm, with mechanisms for investigation, mitigation and resolution.
The sector regulator noted that, at present, AI is increasingly being integrated into telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services.

"With a view to ensuring consistent and responsible implementation of the India AI Governance Guidelines in the telecommunication sector, and to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem, TRAI has decided to frame guidelines on responsible use of AI in telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services after following stakeholders' consultation," TRAI said.

articles.title: Google parent Alphabet’s shares plunge 12.6% as investors question returns from AI spending
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Company reports 25% revenue growth, but quarterly infrastructure spending crosses $51 billion; lower advertising revenue from AI-powered Search queries adds to concerns

Shares of Google parent Alphabet fell 12.64% on the Nasdaq on Thursday (October 29, 2026), closing at $283.82. The decline wiped out about $482 billion in the company’s market value, marking its worst one-day fall since it began trading in 2004, according to reports.
Alphabet shares remained under pressure in Friday’s (October 30, 2026) pre-market trading, slipping a further 0.42% to $282.64, according to Yahoo Finance.
The sell-off came after the company reported its quarterly results, renewing concerns about whether its heavy investments in artificial intelligence (AI) will generate enough returns.

Alphabet’s revenue grew 25% year-on-year to $127.6 billion in the quarter ended September 30. Its net profit fell to $26.5 billion from $35 billion a year earlier, largely due to losses on its equity investments. However, earnings from its business operations rose 30% to $40.6 billion.

Google Cloud was a bright spot. Its revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. The division’s operating income rose to $11.1 billion from $3.6 billion. Alphabet attributed the growth to demand for AI infrastructure and solutions, as well as its core cloud services.

But the investment needed to support this growth is putting pressure on the company’s cash flow. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditure in the September quarter, mainly on data centres, servers and networking equipment. The company said most of this spending went towards technical infrastructure to support its AI investments.

Alphabet generated $42.3 billion in cash from its business operations during the quarter. Since its capital expenditure was higher than the cash generated, it reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion.

Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said infrastructure spending was a major reason for the negative free cash flow. She also pointed to inventory being built up for sales of Google’s own AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), and a $5.2-billion payment relating to a European Commission fine.

Alphabet retained its capital expenditure guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion for 2026. The $51.4 billion spent in the September quarter was roughly a quarter of its projected full-year expenditure. Ms. Ashkenazi said capital expenditure would increase significantly in 2027, indicating that the high spending is likely to continue.

Investors are also watching how AI is changing Google’s main Search advertising business. Revenue from Google Search and related advertising grew 12% to $63.35 billion in the quarter, slower than the 17% growth in the previous quarter. This is part of Google’s total advertising revenue of $82 billion, which also includes advertisements on YouTube and the Google Network.

articles.title: Germans to join Europe's youth protest wave
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In Germany, about 150,000 people have so far registered to turn out on October 31 in around 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne, for protests led by a group dubbed "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!).

Tens of thousands of young Germans are set to demonstrate on Saturday (October 31, 2026), the latest in a wave of protests across Europe led by youths who complain political elites are ignoring their concerns.
From France to Italy and Spain, young protesters have taken to the streets in recent weeks to make their voices heard, with demonstrations sometimes degenerating into serious violence.

In Germany, about 150,000 people have so far registered to turn out on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in around 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne, for protests led by a group dubbed "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!).

While the movement has stressed it rejects all violence, police are taking no chances and are deploying thousands of officers, while some luxury jewellery shops and clothing stores are boarding up their windows to ward off potential looters.

The protest movement has a range of complaints, from high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts, and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians deciding on policies with apparently little regard for the younger generation.

"We are young people who no longer want to sit back and watch while decisions are made about our future without us being heard," said a statement from the group, which describes itself as a non-partisan alliance.
"Wherever we look, we see crises and hardly any prospects for us."
Spending cuts are being made in areas ranging from education to culture and healthcare, they say.
"The cuts are being made at our expense, while big corporations continue to profit and billions flow into rearmament."
They are also unhappy with Germany's bid to boost its military through a new voluntary service model, and fear that mandatory conscription could be reintroduced.

articles.title: Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries, Russia says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: There was no immediate comment from Ukraine
Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries after a brief pause, Russia's deputy prime minister said Friday, warning the strikes could reduce Moscow's planned diesel exports.
U.S. President Donald Trump had been pressuring Kyiv for weeks to stop such attacks, blaming them for the rising cost of diesel.
Analysts have linked rising fuel prices to the war the United States and Israel launched against Iran in February.

"There was an attack overnight on Russian oil-processing facilities... specifically, three oil refineries and one gas-chemical complex," Russia's deputy prime minister for energy issues, Alexander Novak, told a reporter from state TV.
"We had a lull that lasted a certain time, but today the attacks on oil refineries resumed," he added.

Videos published by Russian Telegram channels purported to show smoke billowing from an oil refinery in Russia's Samara region -- located 800 kilometres from the Ukrainian border -- following a drone attack overnight.
Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said on Telegram that two men had been killed in a Ukrainian drone strike.

articles.title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts under Kremlin pressure
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Founded in 1993 after the collapse of the Soviet Union, Novaya Gazeta was one of Russia's most reputable and renowned organisations reporting and documenting human rights abuses.

articles.title: China denies spying on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips, designed by industry leader Nvidia and used to train and run AI models
Beijing dismissed as "groundless speculation" on Friday (October 30, 2026) a report that said Jensen Huang, head of U.S. chip giant Nvidia, was the target of a Chinese spy plot.

The article by The New York Times , published on Thursday (October 29, 2026), said that U.S. intelligence officials concluded that a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company had been funnelling information to Beijing.
"The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing.

China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips, designed by industry leader Nvidia and used to train and run AI models.
The data centre company, Megaspeed, was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.
But the executive Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the New York Times said.
That could have given her insights into U.S. President Donald Trump's thinking around AI, an issue likely to arise during talks with China's President Xi Jinping next month.
Mr. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the report said.
Nvidia is the world's most valuable company thanks to the global drive to build data centres packed with specialist computer chips and other hardware that runs AI systems.
An Nvidia spokesperson told AFP on Friday (October 30, 2026) that Megaspeed was like any other regional customer and "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: An Nvidia spokesperson told AFP on Friday (October 30, 2026) that Megaspeed was like any other regional customer and "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected".

articles.title: Thousands of students, workers protest in Italy under heavy security
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Marches were held in dozens of cities up and down the country, including in Bologna, Genoa, Naples, and Turin — where a few minor skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of the protest

Thousands of students and workers took to the streets across Italy on Friday (October 30, 2026), calling for more school funding and relief from the soaring cost of living, amid a high police presence to avert possible clashes.

Friday's (October 30, 2026) Italy-wide protest comes after weeks of demonstrations, led by students who have set up tent camps and occupied schools to make their demands heard, fuelled by similar movements in nearby France and Spain.

A general strike called by Italy's USB trade union attracted thousands of workers to Friday's (October 30, 2026) protests, including truck drivers, taxi drivers, and farmers who have rallied in recent weeks over the spike in fuel prices and to oppose rising defence spending.

Marches were held in dozens of cities up and down the country, including in Bologna, Genoa, Naples, and Turin — where a few minor skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of the protest.
In Rome, university student Beatrice Chilelli told AFP students were "at a breaking point".

"They can't afford to pay exorbitant tuition fees, and rent... which weighs heavily on their parents' shoulders," said the 21-year-old, citing student housing in Rome that could reach 1,200 euros per month for a single room.

Thousands of people left Rome's central Termini train station, accompanied by two tractors and a taxi, making their way past the Colosseum as they waved flags, unfurled banners and shouted into megaphones.
An AFP photographer witnessed a heavy police presence outside the Economy Ministry, which the procession passed by.
"We need more houses, not bombs!" sang one group in the crowd, as a troupe of protesters gave a brief performance imitating terrified civilians in a Gaza bombing raid.

The Milan protest also began at the central train station, but then headed outside the city — far from the centre where young vandals had looted stores, destroyed property, and clashed with police two weeks ago after another sanctioned cost-of-living demonstration.

articles.title: Will not enforce circular on hospital medicine price disclosure for now: Karnataka government to HC
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The circular mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

The State government on Friday (October 30) told the Karnataka High Court that it would not insist, for now, on the implementation of the circular which mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

An undertaking in this regard was given to the court on behalf of the State’s Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) during the hearing of a petition filed by Private Hospitals and Nursing Homes Association, Bengaluru, and a private hospital. The petitioners have challenged the legality of the October 1 circular.

Justice C.M. Pooncha, before whom the petition came up for hearing, has adjourned further hearing on the petition till November 12 after recording the undertaking given by an Additional Advocate General on instruction from the officials of the FSDA.

The government also informed the court that “the officials concerned are in the process of having a re-look at the circular dated October 1, 2026, and will not enforce the mandate of the circular till November 12, the next date of hearing on the petition”.
The undertaking was given while requesting the court not to stay the circular to allow the government to re-examine the issues raised by the petitioners.

It was contended on behalf of the petitioners that the FSDA had no statutory power to impose such conditions for disclosure of purchase price, which is a commercial agreement between the sellers and buyers that vary depending on suppliers, purchase quantity, discounts, credit arrangements and other factors.

Mandating disclosure of purchase price would result in exposing confidential commercial arrangements between the suppliers and health establishments, it has been contented in the petition, while pointing out that the circular was issued sans adequate consultations with the stakeholders, even though the circular has direct implications on their finance.

The circular mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

The State government on Friday (October 30) told the Karnataka High Court that it would not insist, for now, on the implementation of the circular which mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

An undertaking in this regard was given to the court on behalf of the State’s Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) during the hearing of a petition filed by Private Hospitals and Nursing Homes Association, Bengaluru, and a private hospital. The petitioners have challenged the legality of the October 1 circular.

Justice C.M. Pooncha, before whom the petition came up for hearing, has adjourned further hearing on the petition till November 12 after recording the undertaking given by an Additional Advocate General on instruction from the officials of the FSDA.

The government also informed the court that “the officials concerned are in the process of having a re-look at the circular dated October 1, 2026, and will not enforce the mandate of the circular till November 12, the next date of hearing on the petition”.

The undertaking was given while requesting the court not to stay the circular to allow the government to re-examine the issues raised by the petitioners.

It was contended on behalf of the petitioners that the FSDA had no statutory power to impose such conditions for disclosure of purchase price, which is a commercial agreement between the sellers and buyers that vary depending on suppliers, purchase quantity, discounts, credit arrangements and other factors.

Mandating disclosure of purchase price would result in exposing confidential commercial arrangements between the suppliers and health establishments, it has been contented in the petition, while pointing out that the circular was issued sans adequate consultations with the stakeholders, even though the circular has direct implications on their finance.

fullParagraphs: India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan

Indian drug regulators ordered Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to stop manufacturing, selling and distributing ophthalmic products made at its Assam facility after finding ‌failure in its quality management system, documents reviewed by Reuters showed.

The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation and ​the office of Drugs Controller Assam ordered the shutdown on August 20 after a joint federal-state inspection of ⁠the facility identified lapses in the system meant to ensure product quality and safety, following Sun Pharma’s move in July to voluntarily recall about 11 eye-care brands.

India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan.

articles.title: Two held over death of cheetah; firearm as yet untraced
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Two people have been arrested in connection with the killing of a male cheetah cub at the Kuno National Park, officials said on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A senior wildlife official told The Hindu that two people had been arrested after questioning. “The arrest has been made by a special task force formed for the purpose under the Arms Act, after which the accused were produced before a court. They are currently in police remand, and we will take custody soon,” the official said, requesting anonymity.

“The case will be solved very soon, and we will reveal everything in a day or two. At the moment, multiple teams are at work,” the official said adding that more than five forest personnel had been suspended.

Another senior wildlife official, however, said that the two persons had been detained on Thursday (October 29) evening while the weapon, believed to be a country-made bharmar gun, is yet to be recovered.

“Several people in villages near the spot where the cub was found have been questioned so far and based on that two locals were detained last night [Thursday]. They were arrested today. Searches have also been conducted in the area to find the gun,” the official said, adding that the accused were being questioned about the circumstances of the incident and the firearm used.
Earlier on Thursday (October 29), officials had said that investigating teams have been scanning a large area, mapping the cub’s movement over 15-20 days based on its tracking radio-collar.
The probe is being led by a four-member special task force formed by the State Government along with the State Tiger Strike Force

Officials suspect that the weapon used in the shooting is “a country-made bharmar gun”, a traditional single-shot, muzzle-loading smoothbore firearm that is popular is the rural and forest parts of the region.

The 19-month-old cub, KNG22, an offspring of South African cheetah Nirva, had been found with five gunshot injuries in Sheopur forest division on October 25 and died during treatment on October 27 in Jabalpur. This was the first instance of a cheetah being shot since Project Cheetah, a reintroduction programme for the species, was launched in September, 2022.

articles.title: Infosys opens 1.1 million sq.ft. new block at Pocharam campus in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The new facility will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, the IT major said after the inauguration by Deputy CM Bhatti, IT Minister Sridhar Babu
IT major Infosys announced expansion of its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with the inauguration of a 1.1 million sq.ft. software development block on Friday.

Spread across 450 acres, its campus in Pocharam currently houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq.ft. of built-up area. The new block will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, Infosys said after the inauguration in which Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, IT and Industries Minister D.Sridhar Babu participated.

The expansion of the Pocharam campus by Infosys marks another important milestone for Telangana, which has established itself as a global technology destination, supported by world-class infrastructure, skilled talent and a thriving innovation ecosystem, the Deputy CM said.

“Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad’s position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy,” he was quoted in a release issued by Infosys. The expansion of the facility will create opportunities for the youth to participate in the next wave of technology-led growth, said Mr.Vikramarka, who is also Minister for Finance, Planning and Energy.

The Pocharam Development Centre supports global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, Life Sciences and manufacturing. The expansion will further strengthen the company’s capabilities in AI, Cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services, Infosys said, without sharing investment on the new facility.

Chief Financial Officer of Infosys Jayesh Sanghrajka said Hyderabad has played a pivotal role in the company’s growth and the expansion of the Pocharam campus reflects its continued commitment to the region.

As enterprises accelerate adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub bringing together world-class talent, advanced infrastructure and deep capabilities to help clients drive innovation...”, he said.

On the features of the new facility, Infosys said it incorporates energy-efficient radiant cooling, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater reuse and natural daylight-filled spaces. It also features flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities to support a modern, hybrid work environment.

articles.title: Quantum tech can help solve complex problems: Jnan Yalla
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Qiskit Fall Fest inaugurated at Visvesvaraya Technological University in Belagavi

“Quantum computing is not merely the next step in computer technology. It is a technology that can bring about a significant transformation in our ability to solve complex problems,” according to Research Officer in the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Central government Jnan Yalla.
He was speaking after inaugurating the Qiskit Fall Fest organised by Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) in association with IBM on Jnana Sangama in Belagavi on Friday.

“Quantum technology will open up immense opportunities in the fields of healthcare, drug discovery, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, climate change and the development of new material. India is also taking significant steps towards strengthening its research and development capabilities in the field of quantum technology,” he said.

“As engineering students, you should not look at this technology merely as a subject but consider it an opportunity to shape the future. You have the potential to gain global recognition through innovative ideas, a research-oriented mindset and continuous learning,” he told students.
VTU Vice-Chancellor S. Vidyashankar urged students to cultivate curiosity and undertake research with determination.

“Everyone should work together to create something new and shape tomorrow’s technology. We are organising such conferences to introduce students to quantum technology, which is a technology of the future, and to encourage them to study it in depth. Students should make the best use of these opportunities,” he said.

“Quantum computing has the potential to bring about significant changes in future technology. In particular, quantum algorithms offer new opportunities to make artificial intelligence and machine learning processes faster and more efficient,” IBM Engineer A. Janani said.
As part of the programme, students were given opportunities to find solutions to problems through poster presentations and a hackathon.
Several technical sessions were also held. A report on the activities of the Quantum Club was released.
Registrar (Evaluation) U.J. Ujwal, faculty member Harish Bendigeri, VTU Quantum Club Student Chair Karthik Rao and others were present.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.
• Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court flags irony: Law meant to curb red tapism bogged down it
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, noting that none of the present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law

Noticing delays from 466 days to 1,099 days in filling appeals against judgments, the High Court of Karnataka has said that the State government enacted the Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, “to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of this law.”

A Division Bench comprising Justice M. Nagaprasanna and Justice Hema Kulkarni made these observations on the four appeals filed by the State government challenging verdicts of a single judge related to service of certain employees in the Karnataka State Law University.

Apart from various judgments of the apex court on delay in filling appeals by the State authorities, the State-enacted Act of 2023 clearly prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, while pointing out that that none of present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law on conduct of litigation.

“The time limits prescribed for movement of files, securing opinions, and taking decisions appear to have been thrown to the winds. The State, which enacted the law to bring order and accountability into governmental litigation, has itself failed to demonstrate fidelity to its mandate. The irony is unmistakable: the State enacted a law to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of the law, Bench observed.

The Bench noted that the explanations offered for the delays — files moving from table to table, correspondence passing from officer to officer, legal opinions being sought and documents collected — merely chronicled administrative activity without establishing sufficient cause to condone the delay in filling of the appeal.

“The State is expected to be a model litigant, not a privileged procrastinator. Its obligation is to uphold the rule of law, not to seek exceptions from its operation,” the Bench said while observing that “a law enacted by the State cannot remain a mere ornament in the statute book, commanding obedience from everyone except its own author.

Stating that applications filed by the State government explaining reason for the enormous delay “disclose no exceptional circumstance, no compelling impediment and no credible explanation that could constitute sufficient cause for the extraordinary delays,” the Bench said, while observing that “what is presented as an explanation is, in substance, an assortment of administrative excuses; what is sought as judicial indulgence would, if granted, amount to judicial endorsement of bureaucratic apathy.”
Terming one of the applications a “verbatim reproduction” of another, the Bench said a “copy-and-paste explanation cannot become a passport to condonation of delay”.

articles.title: Unmarried rural youth in Maharashtra plan Statewide stir for government help in getting brides
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Core demands of the youth planning to protest include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce

It is not the inflation, unemployment, deletion of names from the voters’ list or corruption that is simmering in rural Maharashtra youth who are gearing up for an agitation. Unlike other Gen Z across India, these youth have an unusual demand – get us brides to marry.

“We are planning not only a Statewide but a nationwide network of boys who are not getting brides to marry and plan a massive agitation,” Kisan Nanaware, a 28-year-old youth from Solapur, told The Hindu .

Mr. Nanaware came into the limelight after he held a dharna demanding bride at the District Collector’s office in September. He fears he may suffer the same fate as thousands of men in rural Solapur in western Maharashtra, pointing out that the issue stretches far beyond men in their early 30s, with some in their 40s and 50s having given up hope of finding a partner.

Youth such as Mr. Nanaware argue that the State must issue an official resolution detailing steps to assist those who are unmarried. Their core demands include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce. He warns that if authorities fail to act, the movement could take an aggressive turn.
The politicians who have been facing various kinds of agitations are now facing heat of the unmarried youth.

What was supposed to be a standard campaign stop for the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections in Ashti, Beed district (Marathwada region), took a dramatic turn when an agitated young man seized the microphone from local organisers and voiced an issue cutting across rural Maharashtra for which he wanted an immediate answer from the leaders. “Keep aside all other problems and look at our condition,” he demanded, speaking to a crowd of ruling alliance leaders gathered for the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituency elections held on October 23. “Many of us, including me, have crossed 30 or 32 and still we are not getting brides. Solve this problem first!”

Leaders of the BJP-led ruling coalition were not entirely surprised by the outburst. Behind the scenes, politicians have been monitoring simmering anger among rural men who find themselves systematically rejected by prospective brides and their families due to falling farm incomes, lack of steady employment, and a skewed gender ratio.

Maharashtra recorded a sex ratio of 899 girls per 1,000 boys during the 2022-24 period, marginally improving from 896 girls in 2012-14 but well below the national average of 918 girls, according to the latest Sample Registration System Statistical Report.

From Ministers to leaders across party lines, veteran leader Sharad Pawar to local gram panchayat sarpanches, young boys are now raising one simple question, “What about our marriage?” No one has answer to this.

“If not leaders, who is going to answer? At least they must solve one problem and this is the pressing one,” said 32-year-old Avinash Shende from Yavatmal in Vidarbha region. Along with farming, he is working on a contract with a private cleaning agency and has not completed his graduation. He added that like him other youth in the region are now galvanising support to take up this issue at the State level. He says the movement would start from gram sabhas in villages.

Core demands of the youth planning to protest include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce

It is not the inflation, unemployment, deletion of names from the voters’ list or corruption that is simmering in rural Maharashtra youth who are gearing up for an agitation. Unlike other Gen Z across India, these youth have an unusual demand – get us brides to marry.

“We are planning not only a Statewide but a nationwide network of boys who are not getting brides to marry and plan a massive agitation,” Kisan Nanaware, a 28-year-old youth from Solapur, told The Hindu .

Mr. Nanaware came into the limelight after he held a dharna demanding bride at the District Collector’s office in September. He fears he may suffer the same fate as thousands of men in rural Solapur in western Maharashtra, pointing out that the issue stretches far beyond men in their early 30s, with some in their 40s and 50s having given up hope of finding a partner.

Youth such as Mr. Nanaware argue that the State must issue an official resolution detailing steps to assist those who are unmarried. Their core demands include setting up an all-religion marriage registration bureau under the Social Welfare Department, providing direct financial assistance, creating steady rural employment, and guaranteeing remunerative prices for farm produce. He warns that if authorities fail to act, the movement could take an aggressive turn.

The politicians who have been facing various kinds of agitations are now facing heat of the unmarried youth.

What was supposed to be a standard campaign stop for the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections in Ashti, Beed district (Marathwada region), took a dramatic turn when an agitated young man seized the microphone from local organisers and voiced an issue cutting across rural Maharashtra for which he wanted an immediate answer from the leaders. “Keep aside all other problems and look at our condition,” he demanded, speaking to a crowd of ruling alliance leaders gathered for the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituency elections held on October 23. “Many of us, including me, have crossed 30 or 32 and still we are not getting brides. Solve this problem first!”

Leaders of the BJP-led ruling coalition were not entirely surprised by the outburst. Behind the scenes, politicians have been monitoring simmering anger among rural men who find themselves systematically rejected by prospective brides and their families due to falling farm incomes, lack of steady employment, and a skewed gender ratio.

Maharashtra recorded a sex ratio of 899 girls per 1,000 boys during the 2022-24 period, marginally improving from 896 girls in 2012-14 but well below the national average of 918 girls, according to the latest Sample Registration System Statistical Report.

From Ministers to leaders across party lines, veteran leader Sharad Pawar to local gram panchayat sarpanches, young boys are now raising one simple question, “What about our marriage?” No one has answer to this.

“If not leaders, who is going to answer? At least they must solve one problem and this is the pressing one,” said 32-year-old Avinash Shende from Yavatmal in Vidarbha region. Along with farming, he is working on a contract with a private cleaning agency and has not completed his graduation. He added that like him other youth in the region are now galvanising support to take up this issue at the State level. He says the movement would start from gram sabhas in villages.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At least 17 districts of southern Odisha affected by heavy rainfall due to cyclonic storm Arnab; Andhra Pradesh records five deaths as CM Naidu announces relief measures

A day after various parts of Telangana received rain under the impact of cyclonic storm Arnab, isolated places in 12 districts are likely to receive thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds on Thursday (October 29). The very severe cyclonic storm crossed Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning, before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm.

The 12 districts where thunderstorms have been forecast are Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda districts, as per the India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre’s latest weather bulletin.

With severe cyclonic storm Arnab making landfall along the Andhra coast, rainfall activity is likely to ease considerably across Keralam. With the rains subsiding, daytime temperatures are expected to rise noticeably across the State. The dry spell is likely to persist until another weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal, with the mercury expected to climb during the intervening period.

Cyclone Arnab brought back grim memories of ‘Cyclone Hudhud’, which battered the city 12 years ago. Although ‘Arnab’ was less severe and did not make landfall in the city, the strong winds through the night, extensive damage to the city’s green cover, uprooted electric poles, prolonged power outages and disrupted mobile network connectivity reminded residents of the destruction caused by Hudhud in October 2014.

Residents took to social media to compare their experiences of the two cyclones. People recalled sleepless nights, prolonged power cuts and following the district administration’s instructions to remain indoors unless faced with an emergency.
Cyclone Arnab triggers memories of Hudhud’s 2014 destruction in Vizag, with power outages, uprooted trees, and renewed warnings.

Telangana Deputy Chief Minister and Energy Minister Bhatti Vikramarka spoke to Andhra Pradesh Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar over the phone on Wednesday to enquire about the impact of Cyclone Arnab.

Mr. Vikramarka assured Andhra Pradesh of the Telangana government’s full support in dealing with the situation. He said Telangana was ready to provide personnel and essential materials for restoring the damaged power supply infrastructure, if required.

Mr. Ravi Kumar briefed Mr. Vikramarka on the relief and restoration operations being carried out under the guidance of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and thanked the Telangana government for its support.

Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has postponed polling for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections from November 3 to November 5 because the counting of votes for the urban local body (ULB) elections is to be done on November 3 under the revised schedule.

fullParagraphs: Elector-to-population ratio released officially by Karnataka CEO shows under-enrolment of about 64.5 lakh electors, of whom roughly 38.41 lakh are in the 18 to 29 age group.

Around 64.5 lakh electors are potentially missing from the final electoral rolls of Karnataka released after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), based on the Elector-to-Population (E-to-P) ratio of 66.11 released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO).

The State’s E-to-P ratio quoted in the CEO’s statements was calculated as the ratio between the total number of electors on the rolls and the estimated population in 2026 in all age groups, including those below 18 years of age and not eligible to vote.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

articles.title: Bengaluru-based Nature Classrooms releases new butterfly migration game
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Aswathi Asokan, who has conceptualised this new game, talks about its genesis, how it is played and how gamification can help drive conservation

Aswathi Asokan’s journey into the fascinating world of butterflies began in 2019, as a first-year Zoology student at Chennai’s Stella Maris College. “There were a couple of professors in the Zoology Department who were interested in the natural world,” she says, recalling how one of them, Kalpana Jayaraman, was conducting butterfly walks on campus.
“So I began joining those,” says the Bengaluru-based nature educator, researcher, and conservationist who has conceptualised Monsoon Wings, a new butterfly migration and life-cycle game.

As someone who grew up on the verdant IIT Madras campus, she always loved nature, but “it had never got to the point where I was actively identifying species,” she says. Then, on that first campus walk, the professor gave participants a simple printout of the names and pictures of eight or nine common butterflies.

“That made all the difference. Every time I saw a butterfly, I would go back to the printout and try to identify it,” says Aswathi, who developed Monsoon Wings as part of her role as the manager of curriculum development, resources & training at Nature Classrooms, a Bengaluru-based organisation that works with schools and educators to connect learning and the natural world. “I like to think that this was the start of me understanding the power of a tool like that.”

She began noticing butterflies a lot more after that, closely observing their life cycles in the plants around her. At around the same time, she became part of the Chennai Young Naturalists’ Network, a group of young naturalists in Chennai.

Through this group, she met like-minded people, with whom she would go on to co-author a bilingual field guide, Butterflies of Chennai , in 2023. ”The data used to create the guide came from my friend Vikas Madhav, an experienced young naturalist who did nearly 10 years of butterfly documentation work in Chennai before moving to the US,” says Aswathi, who ended up doing a lot of nature education work in Chennai before going on to pursue a master’s in wildlife conservation action from the Bharati Vidyapeeth Institute of Environment Education and Research, Pune.
Blue Tiger butterflies are known for their seasonal migrations, linked to monsoon cycles | Photo Credit: MURALI KUMAR K

All the time spent dabbling in resource creation, including field guides, bingos and posters, has played a tremendous role in shaping this new butterfly game, which has been inspired by the ‘Bird Survivor’ game by Early Bird, an initiative by the Education and Public Engagement Programme of the Nature Conservation Foundation. “We were using this game extensively in our Nature Classrooms workshops, and I got familiar with it,” Aswathi says, explaining that this game, in turn, took inspiration from one developed by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.

While working with Nature Classrooms, Aswathi was also actively working with Sunnyside Learning School in Chennai, running biodiversity exploration programmes for its students. “I was trying to plan a session around butterflies for the Sunnyside kids, and since the mechanics are quite similar, I thought I could adapt the bird migration game to a butterfly context and see if it works.”

While bird and monarch butterfly migration are well known and widely discussed, butterfly migration in India is so common right around us, yet few people know about it, Aswathi says. “That’s why I wanted to create a resource and incorporate that into the kids’ session.”

Through this group, she met like-minded people, with whom she would go on to co-author a bilingual field guide, Butterflies of Chennai , in 2023. ”The data used to create the guide came from my friend Vikas Madhav, an experienced young naturalist who did nearly 10 years of butterfly documentation work in Chennai before moving to the US,” says Aswathi, who ended up doing a lot of nature education work in Chennai before going on to pursue a master’s in wildlife conservation action from the Bharati Vidyapeeth Institute of Environment Education and Research, Pune.

articles.title: India must build a holistic care system
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. With an ageing population, the need for accessible care services will only grow.

Yet care rarely features in India’s growth strategy. For a Viksit Bharat 2047, the question is not only how to expand women’s economic participation, but how to build the care system that makes such participation possible. The Anganwadi network, strengthened through Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, anchors early childhood care and nutrition. Palna, under Mission Shakti, supports crèches, while Mission Vatsalya, social security and provisions for persons with disabilities and senior citizens address other needs. The challenge is architecture, not ambition. Four gaps stand out.

First, fragmentation. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework. This can leave gaps such as crèches that close before factory shifts end or eldercare needs that fall outside of existing schemes.

Second, coverage. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates that 9–10 million women in low-income urban households need childcare. Similarly for eldercare, 24% of older persons face limitations in daily activities, while national data on service availability and coverage remain limited.

Third, the workforce. Care depends on frontline workers; from Anganwadi workers to home-based caregivers and domestic workers — many of whom remain inadequately remunerated or engaged on an honorary basis. Building on NITI Aayog’s proposals, clear standards, certification, decent working conditions, social protection and career pathways would recognise care as skilled and paid work.

Finally, financing and norms. Care is still budgeted as welfare rather than investment, and workplace policies assume that caregiving is women’s work. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) recommends statutory paid paternity leave in the private sector.

Comparable economies are building their own care ecosystems. Colombia’s 2025 National Care Policy brings 34 government entities under one framework. Brazil’s 2024 National Care Policy and 2025 National Care Plan set up inter-Ministerial committees to steer implementation. In Nepal, care mapping was used to fund care pilots.

In India, NITI Aayog’s Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047 report proposes a National Caregiving Council to strengthen coordination. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is consulting States and Union Territories; its May 2026 national workshop discussed a National Care Economy Mission with inter-Ministerial governance, aligned financing and shared data. State-level care roadmaps can make this practical. States can map needs, services and demographic trends, identify gaps in childcare, eldercare and disability support, and prepare costed plans with clear responsibilities.

articles.title: Extremely harmful to Indian democracy: Rijiju slams Naseeruddin Shah's 'dimagi naxal' video
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a video posted on Facebook, a visibly angry Naseeruddin Shah came out in support of Jamia Millia Islamia students, who have been protesting for the restoration of the students' union, and called himself a "dimagi naxal"

Union Minister Kiren Rijiju has said Naseeruddin Shah is a "dangerous urban dimagi naxal" whose views are "extremely harmful" to Indian democracy, after the actor posted a video accusing the Centre of trying to destroy the education system.
In a post on X on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Minister for minority affairs said he used to respect Mr. Shah, but came to know of his "real character" very late.

In a video posted on Facebook on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), a visibly angry Mr. Shah came out in support of Jamia Millia Islamia students, who have been protesting for the restoration of the students' union, and called himself a "dimagi naxal".

He accused the BJP-led central government of trying to destroy the education system and break the "courage of the country's youth". Shah was also wearing a "dimagi naxal" pin that he showed to the camera.
Mr. Rijiju criticised the actor, saying, "I thought Naseeruddin Shah was just an ordinary actor. I used to respect & like him... I never knew that he was a dangerous urban Dimagi Naxal."
"I came to know about his real character very late. (His views are) extremely harmful to India's democracy," he added.

The term 'dimagi naxal' was first used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Independence Day address. He described "dimagi naxals" as those who have allegedly entrenched themselves in the system and continue to pose a threat to society by manipulating policies.
Speaking to PTI Videos, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC also questioned Mr. Shah over his remarks.

She said, "The question is whether Naseeruddin Shah is ACP Rathod or Gulam Hassan of 'Sarfarosh'. He talks about urban naxalism, supporting the tukde-tukde gang, anti-national movements. The question to you, sir, with utmost respect, is do you believe in pro-India sloganeering or anti-India."
Shah played the antagonist, covert operator Gulfam Hassan, in the Aamir Khan-starrer action drama "Sarfarosh". Khan played the role of the protagonist, ACP Ajay Singh Rathod, in the 1999 superhit.

Mr. Rijiju criticised the actor, saying, "I thought Naseeruddin Shah was just an ordinary actor. I used to respect & like him... I never knew that he was a dangerous urban Dimagi Naxal."

"I came to know about his real character very late. (His views are) extremely harmful to India's democracy," he added.

The term 'dimagi naxal' was first used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Independence Day address. He described "dimagi naxals" as those who have allegedly entrenched themselves in the system and continue to pose a threat to society by manipulating policies.

Speaking to PTI Videos, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC also questioned Mr. Shah over his remarks.

She said, "The question is whether Naseeruddin Shah is ACP Rathod or Gulam Hassan of 'Sarfarosh'. He talks about urban naxalism, supporting the tukde-tukde gang, anti-national movements. The question to you, sir, with utmost respect, is do you believe in pro-India sloganeering or anti-India."

Shah played the antagonist, covert operator Gulfam Hassan, in the Aamir Khan-starrer action drama "Sarfarosh". Khan played the role of the protagonist, ACP Ajay Singh Rathod, in the 1999 superhit.
