articles.title: Postal Department organises awareness rally in Yadgir to promote integrity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ​Flagging off the rally, Assistant Superintendent of Post Offices (Yadgir division) Krishna Mohite stressed that honesty, morality, and accountability form the foundation of individual and societal prosperity

​The Yadgir Postal Division organised an awareness rally under the theme ‘Integrity for Prosperity’ in Yadgir on October 28, emphasising the need for a corruption-free administration and high ethical standards in public life.
The rally, which commenced at the divisional postal office near Ambedkar Circle in Yadgir city, passed through key routes before concluding at Babu Jagjivan Ram Circle.
Postal personnel and officers spread the message of transparency among the public and government staff.

​Flagging off the rally, Assistant Superintendent of Post Offices (Yadgir division) Krishna Mohite stressed that honesty, morality, and accountability form the foundation of individual and societal prosperity. “A corruption-free society and good governance can only be achieved when every individual discharges their duties with utmost dedication and responsibility,” he said.

​Speakers at the event urged government employees to adopt strong ethical principles in daily administration, maintain transparency while interacting with people, and ensure responsible utilisation of government resources.
​Assistant Superintendent of Post Offices Lakshmikant Kodli, Yadgir Postmaster Veeranna Pattar, alongside department personnel Chandrakala, Dattatri, and Mallikarjun, were present.

articles.title: Kerala HC quashes cheating case against Nivin Pauly, director Abrid Shine after out-of-court settlement in dispute over film rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Complaint against the duo was filed following financial dispute related to making of Action Hero Biju 2. The complainant alleged that after entering into an agreement to produce the film, its overseas rights were sold to another party without his knowledge
The Kerala High Court has quashed the cheating case against actor Nivin Pauly and director Abrid Shine, registered with the Thalayolaparambu police station.
Justice P.V. Balakrishnan noted that the parties had reached an out-of-court settlement in the dispute that had led to the registration of the case.

The complainant, P.S. Shamnas had filed the complaint with the Thalayolaparambu police following a financial dispute related to the making of the film Action Hero Biju 2 . articles.title: Study in Keralam sheds light on link between gut bacteria, Parkinson’s disease
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Researchers from CUSAT and SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram, find significant differences between gut bacteria of Parkinson’s patients and those of healthy individuals

Trillions of bacteria living in the human gut may play a role in Parkinson’s disease, a brain disorder that causes tremors, stiffness, and slowed movement, according to a new study involving patients from Keralam.

Researchers from the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT) and the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram, found significant differences between the gut bacteria of Parkinson’s patients and those of healthy individuals. The findings were published online in npj Parkinson’s Disease , an international scientific journal.

Parkinson’s disease occurs when nerve cells in the brain that produce dopamine, a chemical that helps control movement, gradually die. Scientists have long suspected that the gut and brain communicate continuously, and that an imbalance in gut bacteria could contribute to inflammation affecting the brain. Studies have shown that non-motor symptoms, including constipation and other gastrointestinal problems, can appear years before the tremors begin in Parkinson’s patients.

The study involved 65 Parkinson’s patients attending SCTIMST’s Comprehensive Care Centre for Movement Disorders and 65 healthy individuals, most of whom were the patients’ spouses. Spouses were included as healthy individuals for comparison, as they were more likely to share similar diets and living conditions.

Researchers analysed stool samples using metagenomic sequencing (16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing), a technique that identifies the bacteria present and helps assess their potential functions in the gut. They found higher levels of bacteria potentially associated with inflammation and lower levels of beneficial bacteria that produce short-chain fatty acids, which help maintain the gut lining healthy and regulate the immune system, in Parkinson’s patients.
The researchers suggest that the shift in bacterial communities could weaken the gut barrier and allow inflammation to spread.

“The study found that differences in the abundances of these bacteria were strongly associated with disease severity and other clinical features of Parkinson’s disease,” said Baby Chakrapani P. S., scientist and director of the Centre for Neuroscience at CUSAT. “The findings also suggest that gut bacteria may be linked to disease progression through their influence on processes involving dopamine, glutamate, and GABA, chemicals that play important roles in brain function.”

Funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), the study was conducted by Aneesa P. A., a research associate at CUSAT, under the supervision of Mr. Chakrapani and Dr. Syam Krishnan of SCTIMST.

Gut bacterial composition is influenced by factors such as diet, age, sex, and lifestyle. Differences in these factors, as well as genetics, could explain why studies in different populations have reported inconsistent associations between particular bacteria and Parkinson’s disease.

According to the researchers, this is the first study in an Indian population to integrate gut microbiome composition with its functional role in Parkinson’s disease. The findings could help future research into simple tests for early diagnosis of the disease and treatments aimed at restoring gut health.

articles.title: Delhi Police grants Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan with strict conditions, denies mock impeachment request
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police say no separate request was received for the proposed mock impeachment on October 30 and November 1; rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 cleared subject to conditions, including CCTV surveillance and a ban on marches outside the venue

The Delhi Police on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said they had not received any request seeking permission for a proposed mock “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 30 and November 1, denying reports that permission for the proposed events had been refused.

Speaking to The Hindu, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had sought permission only for a rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, which was granted subject to several conditions. No separate request for a mock impeachment had been received, he said.

As per the permission letter issued by the Central district police, as reported by The Hindu , the rally is scheduled to be held from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1. The police have given a no-objection from the law-and-order perspective, subject to the organisers obtaining prior permission from the land-owning authority.

The conditions include installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic points across the venue, including entry and exit gates, the stage and seating enclosures, along with a control room and five screens as part of the monitoring system. Organisers have also been asked to provide adequate water tankers and toilet facilities, including separate toilets for women, and deploy sufficient volunteers to manage the gathering.

The police have directed the organisers to ensure that the rally remains peaceful and concludes by 5 p.m., with dispersal beginning thereafter. Overnight stays at the venue before or after the rally will not be permitted, and vehicles must be parked at locations designated by the Traffic Unit.

The permission letter also states that no march will be allowed towards any location outside Ramlila Maidan. Organisers have been asked to submit the list of invitees and volunteers, a minute-by-minute programme, and details of buses, including their registration numbers.

The police have further directed the organisers to ensure that no speeches disturb public harmony or contain inflammatory or intimidating content. If any such speech is made, the public address system must be switched off immediately and the speaker removed from the stage.
The letter warns that any breach of the conditions or failure to comply with police directions could lead to legal action against the organisers and revocation of the permission.

Police say no separate request was received for the proposed mock impeachment on October 30 and November 1; rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 cleared subject to conditions, including CCTV surveillance and a ban on marches outside the venue

The Delhi Police on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said they had not received any request seeking permission for a proposed mock “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 30 and November 1, denying reports that permission for the proposed events had been refused.

Speaking to The Hindu, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had sought permission only for a rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, which was granted subject to several conditions. No separate request for a mock impeachment had been received, he said.

As per the permission letter issued by the Central district police, as reported by The Hindu , the rally is scheduled to be held from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1. The police have given a no-objection from the law-and-order perspective, subject to the organisers obtaining prior permission from the land-owning authority.

The conditions include installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic points across the venue, including entry and exit gates, the stage and seating enclosures, along with a control room and five screens as part of the monitoring system. Organisers have also been asked to provide adequate water tankers and toilet facilities, including separate toilets for women, and deploy sufficient volunteers to manage the gathering.

The police have directed the organisers to ensure that the rally remains peaceful and concludes by 5 p.m., with dispersal beginning thereafter. Overnight stays at the venue before or after the rally will not be permitted, and vehicles must be parked at locations designated by the Traffic Unit.

The permission letter also states that no march will be allowed towards any location outside Ramlila Maidan. Organisers have been asked to submit the list of invitees and volunteers, a minute-by-minute programme, and details of buses, including their registration numbers.

The police have further directed the organisers to ensure that no speeches disturb public harmony or contain inflammatory or intimidating content. If any such speech is made, the public address system must be switched off immediately and the speaker removed from the stage.

The letter warns that any breach of the conditions or failure to comply with police directions could lead to legal action against the organisers and revocation of the permission.

fullParagraphs: Seoul accused North Korea of planting mines south of the military demarcation line that caused the September 21 blasts, but Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked

articles.title: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner even as Trump considers new Iran strikes
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The defence official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Mr. Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, a defence official said on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the latest in a series of generals to be ousted and one that comes even as President Donald Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran in the eight-month-long war.

Army Lt Gen Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He is the second general to be ousted from the post, known in military circles as the “J5”, under Mr. Hegseth. His predecessor, Lt Gen Joseph McGee, was forced to retire last October.

The defence official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Mr. Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing. The move was reported earlier by The Atlantic .

A spokesperson for the Joint Staff said “the Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Joint Force extend our deepest gratitude to Lt Gen Brett Sylvia and his family for their 32 years of distinguished service to our nation” and they "wish him and his family the best.”

Typically, the J5 director and their staff are responsible for generating and coordinating military plans with both the chairman of the Joint Chiefs and the President. Mr. Sylvia's firing comes as Mr. Trump has repeatedly floated starting new military operations against Iran.
Mr. Trump has vowed to “finish the job” in Iran after launching the war with Israel eight months ago and said new strikes are an option after the midterm elections next week.

U.S. officials have told several West Asian countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action after Tuesday's (November 3) elections as well as for the possibility that Iran will attempt to retaliate against them, two diplomats briefed on the matter said. They say Mr. Trump has not made a final decision on new strikes.
A third U.S. aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are making their way to the region.

Before arriving at the Joint Staff, Sylvia served as the commander of the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025, according to his official biography, which has now been taken offline. He also previously served as the vice director for the J5.

He is the latest in nearly two dozen generals, admirals and other military leaders to be fired, forced to retire or otherwise depart under Hegseth's tenure — almost all of which have not been publicly explained by the Pentagon.

articles.title: What is ‘human composting’ — how does it work?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: What should happen to your body after you die? It’s hardly a topic you’d bring up over dinner, but it’s a decision that will eventually need to be made, either by you or by those you leave behind.

In Australia, the choice has traditionally been between burial and cremation. However, concerns about environmental impact, limited cemetery space and the desire for more sustainable alternatives have encouraged interest in other approaches.
These include natural burial, water cremation and shrouded cremation — where no coffin is used.

Now, New South Wales has become the first Australian state to pass legislation allowing another option: “human composting”, technically known as natural organic reduction, and legally termed “terramation”. The process uses microorganisms to transform human remains into a compost-like material.
📢 So-called terramation will become legal in NSW, with several MPs revealing they want their own bodies turned into soil after they die. [image or embed]
The idea of turning a human body into compost might sound unusual, or even unsettling. But how does it actually work? Is it a better alternative to existing methods?
To answer these questions, we first need to understand decomposition and its essential role in nature.
Throughout history, humans have developed rituals to protect, preserve and dress the dead. Some want a quick return to the earth, while others seek to preserve the body.
From ancient burial vessels and elaborate tombs to coffins, shrouds and embalming, these practices reflect cultural and religious beliefs. They also affect how bodies decompose.
Decomposition begins shortly after death. As cells break down, microorganisms already living inside the body, along with those from the surrounding environment, begin breaking down its tissues.

articles.title: Building a holistic care system for India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. With an ageing population, the need for accessible care services will only grow.

Yet care is only beginning to feature in India’s growth strategy. For a Viksit Bharat 2047, the question is not only how to expand women’s economic participation, but how to build the care system that makes such participation possible. The Anganwadi network, strengthened through Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, anchors early childhood care and nutrition. Palna, under Mission Shakti, supports crèches, while Mission Vatsalya, social security and provisions for persons with disabilities and senior citizens address other needs. The challenge is architecture, not ambition. Four gaps stand out.

First, fragmentation. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework. This can leave gaps such as crèches that close before factory shifts end or eldercare needs that fall outside of existing schemes.

Second, coverage. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates that 9–10 million women in low-income urban households need childcare. Similarly for eldercare, 24% of older persons face limitations in daily activities, while national data on service availability and coverage remain limited.

Third, the workforce. Care depends on frontline workers; from Anganwadi workers to home-based caregivers and domestic workers — many of whom remain inadequately remunerated or engaged on an honorary basis. Building on NITI Aayog’s proposals, clear standards, certification, decent working conditions, social protection and career pathways would recognise care as skilled and paid work.

Finally, financing and norms. Care is still budgeted as welfare rather than investment, and workplace policies assume that caregiving is women’s work. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) recommends statutory paid paternity leave in the private sector.

Comparable economies are building their own care ecosystems. Colombia’s 2025 National Care Policy brings 34 government entities under one framework. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. With an ageing population, the need for accessible care services will only grow.

Yet care is only beginning to feature in India’s growth strategy. For a Viksit Bharat 2047, the question is not only how to expand women’s economic participation, but how to build the care system that makes such participation possible. The Anganwadi network, strengthened through Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, anchors early childhood care and nutrition. Palna, under Mission Shakti, supports crèches, while Mission Vatsalya, social security and provisions for persons with disabilities and senior citizens address other needs. The challenge is architecture, not ambition. Four gaps stand out.

First, fragmentation. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework. This can leave gaps such as crèches that close before factory shifts end or eldercare needs that fall outside of existing schemes.

Second, coverage. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates that 9–10 million women in low-income urban households need childcare. Similarly for eldercare, 24% of older persons face limitations in daily activities, while national data on service availability and coverage remain limited.

Third, the workforce. Care depends on frontline workers; from Anganwadi workers to home-based caregivers and domestic workers — many of whom remain inadequately remunerated or engaged on an honorary basis. Building on NITI Aayog’s proposals, clear standards, certification, decent working conditions, social protection and career pathways would recognise care as skilled and paid work.

Finally, financing and norms. Care is still budgeted as welfare rather than investment, and workplace policies assume that caregiving is women’s work. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) recommends statutory paid paternity leave in the private sector.

Comparable economies are building their own care ecosystems. Colombia’s 2025 National Care Policy brings 34 government entities under one framework. Brazil’s 2024 National Care Policy and 2025 National Care Plan set up inter-Ministerial committees to steer implementation. In Nepal, care mapping was used to fund care pilots.

In India, NITI Aayog’s Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047 report proposes a National Caregiving Council to strengthen coordination. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is consulting States and Union Territories; its May 2026 national workshop discussed a National Care Economy Mission with inter-Ministerial governance, aligned financing and shared data. State-level care roadmaps can make this practical. States can map needs, services and demographic trends, identify gaps in childcare, eldercare and disability support, and prepare costed plans with clear responsibilities.

articles.title: How the humble salt marsh softens the ocean’s fury
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon

The boundary between land and sea is neither fixed nor clear. The soil does not suddenly stop and give away to a wall of water. Instead, the line is often a salt marsh, where ocean waves break and lose vim as they pass over the marsh’s elevated surface and push against the stems of salt-tolerant plants.

Gujarat is home to India’s largest coastal salt marshes, with smaller areas in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra, among some other places. One 2020 study in Estuarine Coastal and Shelf Science estimated they covered around 290 sq. km in all, and supported wildlife and stabilised coastal sediments. Unfortunately they also face significant threats from expanding aquaculture and coastal development.

As global warming continues, storms become ever stronger and water levels rise, these coastal zones are slowly being acknowledged for the formidable natural buffers they are. But they are being threatened as well, especially their plants, and what might happen if they are gone?

A 2014 study in Nature Geoscience used a wave flume — a long tank filled with water that uses a mechanical paddle to generate waves — to show that the plants of the salt marsh could break waves substantially even when their stems bent or broke.

A new study in Nature by researchers at Wageningen University & Research in the Netherlands took the study a big step further. The team moved 306 sq. metres of a live salt marsh, down to the soil and roots, from the coast of the Dutch Wadden Sea to a 300-metre-long flume at the Deltares Research Institute, capable of creating the world’s largest artificial waves. There, the marsh was tested at different depths against waves measuring 75 cm, 1.25 metres, and 2 metres high over many hours.

The findings were remarkable: the marsh’s elevation fell only 7 mm but at the cost of the flora on the surface losing 75-80% of their biomass and having their stems become shorter by almost half. The researchers concluded the plants’ dense network of roots had helped hold the sediments together. The team also found the plants cut the height of waves 75 cm high by 6-22% but those of waves 2 metres high only by up to 6%.

The team also combined their findings with maps of salt marshes worldwide and modelled the storm surges there. For once in a century storms — the kind climate change is rendering more common these days, like Cyclone Nisarga in 2020 — the team elucidated two kinds of outcomes. Where the incoming waves are at most a metre high, the plants could be expected to cut the height of waves by over 10%, in some instances by as much as 50%. But if the waves got higher, the plants (alone) also became less effective at attenuating them.

Obviously these figures are not a guarantee for every coast everywhere. The study relied on a Dutch marsh dominated by one species of grass ( Elymus athericus ). A different study published this year, in Communications Sustainability , also found that marsh species with more flexible stems often survived extreme waves better than stiffer ones.
Nonetheless, the findings are important: they reinforce the ecological value of salt marshes, including the roots they still hold on exposed coasts.

articles.title: Microsoft beats expectations fueled by Azure cloud business
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce

Microsoft shares popped more than five percent Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, fueled by its Azure cloud computing division which grew by 48 percent in the September quarter.
“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement.
The technology giant recorded $92.3 billion in total revenue and more than $36.6 billion in profit, the company said in a securities filing Wednesday.
Analysts had expected around $90.6 billion in revenue and $35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.

The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence investments.
It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year, after giving seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early in April.
Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.
Earlier this month, Microsoft also announced a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips and will cost more than $2,500.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users do not have to rely solely on remote cloud data centers, where running AI is slower and more expensive.
Microsoft will hold a call with analysts on Wednesday afternoon to discuss its quarterly results.

The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce

Microsoft shares popped more than five percent Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, fueled by its Azure cloud computing division which grew by 48 percent in the September quarter.

“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement.

The technology giant recorded $92.3 billion in total revenue and more than $36.6 billion in profit, the company said in a securities filing Wednesday.

Analysts had expected around $90.6 billion in revenue and $35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.

The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence investments.

It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year, after giving seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early in April.

Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.

Earlier this month, Microsoft also announced a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips and will cost more than $2,500.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users do not have to rely solely on remote cloud data centers, where running AI is slower and more expensive.

Microsoft will hold a call with analysts on Wednesday afternoon to discuss its quarterly results.

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon AI model with cybersecurity focus
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The model is designed to handle complex, long-running engineering and coding tasks

Alphabet’s Google on Wednesday unveiled Gemini 4 ​Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, ‌stepping up competition with ​OpenAI and Anthropic ⁠as the race to build more capable coding and cybersecurity systems intensifies.
The ‌launch comes two weeks after Google ‌introduced Gemini 4 Argon, as ‌the ⁠company expands its Gemini ⁠family of AI models for developers and enterprise customers.
The ‌company said the Carbon model delivers state-of-the-art performance across cybersecurity tasks including vulnerability discovery, ‌exploitation, and software patching.
Google ​said Carbon generates secure code at more ⁠than twice the success rate of Gemini 4 Argon on ‌internal benchmarks.
The model is designed to handle complex, long-running engineering and coding tasks.
Carbon is being made available first ‌to a subset of cybersecurity defenders ​through Google’s Fairwind Program as the company continues testing ⁠safeguards.
Gemini 4 Carbon will ⁠be priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 ‌per million output tokens, matching Gemini 4 Argon’s ​introductory pricing.

articles.title: Hasanamba Temple festival: KSRTC, KSTDC announce 12 tour packages; private operators fully booked
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In view of the historic Hasanamba Temple festival in Hassan, the Karnataka State Tourism Development Corporation (KSTDC), in collaboration with the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) and the Hassan district administration, has launched around 12 tour packages.

The doors of the temple opened on Thursday, and devotees will be allowed for darshan of the goddess from Friday onwards. A senior official from KSTDC said, “The doors of the temple open once a year and this year, it is open up to November 11. During this season, lakhs of tourists including those from other states living in Bengaluru and Mysuru visit this temple. Therefore, our tour packages have been announced not only to promote tourism but boost the local economy of Hassan.”

Under these packages, KSTDC and KSRTC will operate buses from Bengaluru, Mysuru and local places in Hassan. The official explained, “We have currently launched two packages from our side on the occasion of the Hasanamba temple festival. Our buses will operate from Bengaluru and Mysuru. The Bengaluru-Hassan-Bengaluru package is priced at ₹2,300 per person including ₹1,000, the price of the ticket for darshan of the Hasanamba temple. Tourists or devotees can visit Narsimha temple, Nuggehalli Nageshwara temple and finally Hasanamba temple.”

The bus operating from Bengaluru will start at 6 a.m. from Yeshwantpur and return at 10 p.m. Similarly, the KSTDC bus from Mysuru is priced at ₹2,150 per person including the ticket price to the temple. Tourists will get to visit the Hasanamba temple along with the Hoysaleshwara temple in Halebidu and the Chennakeshava temple in Belur before returning to Mysuru.

At the same time, KSRTC has announced 10 bus packages under which Karnataka Sarige, premium AC and Ashwamedha buses are operating, taking tourists to various sightseeing spots, historical monuments and seven temples (’Sapta Maatrikas’) associated with the Hasanamba temple in Hassan. The prices of KSRTC tour packages differ for adults and children in the age group of 5 to 12 years. While the price range for adults starts at ₹500 and goes up to ₹2,500, ticket prices for children start at ₹275 and go up to ₹2,200.
Meanwhile, private tour and travel operators who provide cars, tempo travellers and buses that can accommodate 30 to 40 people have separate packages during this season.

Pruthvi Gowda, a private tour and travel operator, said, “The prices of private cars, TTs and buses vary according to the demand and availability of drivers on a particular day. During the Hasanamba temple festival, most travel operators are fully booked. For instance, November 1 and 2 are weekends and government holidays are completely booked. Tuesdays and Fridays are two days when we are completely booked.”

Mr. Pruthvi added, “The price for a car that can occupy four people is charged somewhere around ₹3,500 to ₹4,500 per day. This includes the diesel money and toll charges. Drivers take people around ten different places including Hasanamba temple, Belur, Halebidu, boating in Yagachi backwaters, Shravanabelagola, Shettihalli Rosary Church, Manjarabad fort, Bisle Ghat and others; it takes one entire day. If there are around 10 to 15 people, then operators charge between ₹5,000 and ₹8,000 for one full day.”

articles.title: Gadag district has 7.94 lakh voters after SIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: There were 9,02,947 registered voters before the Special Intensive Revision of electoral roll in the district
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Gadag district has been completed with 7,94,567 voters on the final electoral roll.

Chairing a meeting at the district administrative complex to announce the final roll and distribute copies to representatives of political parties in Gadag on Wednesday, Deputy Commissioner C.N. Sridhar said that the district had 9,02,947 registered voters before the revision.
The final roll comprises 3,98,385 men, 3,96,139 women and 43 voters from the third gender, he said.
During the revision, officials identified 30,318 deceased voters, 71,280 voters who have permanently shifted residence and 13,537 voters registered in more than one place.
Another 5,192 voters were found absent, while 388 names were removed for other reasons. A total of 1,20,715 entries were deleted from the electoral roll, he said.
Mr. Sridhar said that eligible voters can apply for inclusion of names, correction of names or other details and inclusion of names inadvertently omitted from the roll.
Details of the final electoral roll are available on the Gadag district administration’s official website and the Election Commission of India’s website.
He also distributed copies of the final roll to representatives of political parties.
Additional Deputy Commissioner Durgakesh K.R., Assistant Commissioner Gangappa M. and Deputy Director of Social Welfare Nanda Hanabaratti were among those present.

articles.title: CSIR-NGRI director stresses need for expertise in carbon storage research
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Identifying suitable geological formations for the safe and long-term storage of carbon dioxide will require a combination of scientific expertise, advanced technologies and skilled manpower, said CSIR-National Geophysical Research Institute (CSIR-NGRI) Prakash Kumar, while inaugurating a five-day training programme on ‘Subsurface Characterization of Geological Carbon Storage Sites (SC-GCS)’.

The programme, being conducted under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, aims to build expertise in carbon capture and storage technologies, a key component of India’s efforts to curb greenhouse gas emissions and address climate change.

Addressing participants, Mr. Prakash Kumar highlighted the growing importance of geological carbon storage in achieving the country’s climate goals. The training programme has drawn 14 participants, including four women and 10 men, from academia, industry and independent consulting from organisations and institutions, including NPCIL, Oil India Limited, Kalpra Tech Solutions, Drake AI, Banaras Hindu University, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, NIT Karnataka and Osmania University.

The programme is designed to strengthen technical capacity in the emerging field of geological carbon storage and support the development and deployment of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies in the country. Geological carbon storage is increasingly being viewed as an important strategy for reducing industrial carbon emissions while supporting economic growth.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Fed is expected to keep the rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market economies for foreign investors

The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

articles.title: Pope Leo’s Argentina visit brings renewed scrutiny of clergy abuse scandals
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Victims have expressed frustration over the Vatican’s silence on church proceedings involving priests convicted in criminal courts

Pope Leo’s visit to Argentina comes amid allegations of sexual abuse and other crimes involving Catholic clergy and lay members, with survivors demanding stronger action from the Vatican against those accused or convicted.

Victims have expressed frustration over the Vatican’s silence on church proceedings involving priests convicted in criminal courts. They are demanding that the clergy be defrocked, the Catholic Church’s most severe disciplinary punishment.

The papal visit, initially scheduled for November 8-11, has stirred mixed feelings. Some survivors hope to meet Pope to share their experiences and demand action, while others, including members of a network of clergy abuse survivors, oppose his visit, saying the church has failed to deliver on its promises of “zero tolerance” for abuse. Here are some of the major scandals involving the Catholic Church in Argentina

Pope is scheduled to visit Córdoba province, where priest Alejandro Nicola faces allegations of sexually abusing children at a Catholic school’s kindergarten, mostly in 2025. More than a dozen families have filed complaints. Prosecutors are investigating, while the local church has opened a preliminary inquiry.

Priest Nicola was seen celebrating Mass at Córdoba’s cathedral in July despite the allegations, angering families of the alleged victims. The Pope is expected to visit the cathedral during his trip. Florencia Navarro and Fernanda Agüero, who accuse Priest Nicola of abusing their daughters, criticised church and school authorities for their handling of the allegations.

“I would like him to provide explanations, since they talk so much about protecting the vulnerable,” Mr. Navarro said of the pope. Ms. Agüero said she hoped the Pope’s message would be backed by “concrete actions” rather than words alone.

Cordoba Archbishop Ángel Rossi invoked the priest’s presumption of innocence when questioned about the case. Priest Nicola has not addressed the allegations, telling journalists only that “the lawyers will take care of that.” His defence team has not commented publicly on the case.
A group of 43 women who allege they were subjected to human trafficking and forced labor at Opus Dei centres in Argentina hope to meet the pope in Buenos Aires.

The allegations implicate senior members of the conservative Catholic organisation, including its global leader, Fernando Ocáriz. Three former Opus Dei vicars in South America and a former regional secretary of its women’s section have been formally accused in the investigation, along with Mariano Fazio, the organisation’s second-highest-ranking official.

Prosecutors have requested that the defendants be summoned for questioning, but the judge has not ordered it. They are also investigating claims that the women were recruited as teenagers under false promises and forced to work 12 to 16 hours a day as domestic servants without pay, under conditions of isolation and strict control, between the 1970s and 2015.

Victims have expressed frustration over the Vatican’s silence on church proceedings involving priests convicted in criminal courts

Pope Leo’s visit to Argentina comes amid allegations of sexual abuse and other crimes involving Catholic clergy and lay members, with survivors demanding stronger action from the Vatican against those accused or convicted.

Victims have expressed frustration over the Vatican’s silence on church proceedings involving priests convicted in criminal courts. They are demanding that the clergy be defrocked, the Catholic Church’s most severe disciplinary punishment.

The papal visit, initially scheduled for November 8-11, has stirred mixed feelings. Some survivors hope to meet Pope to share their experiences and demand action, while others, including members of a network of clergy abuse survivors, oppose his visit, saying the church has failed to deliver on its promises of “zero tolerance” for abuse. Here are some of the major scandals involving the Catholic Church in Argentina

Pope is scheduled to visit Córdoba province, where priest Alejandro Nicola faces allegations of sexually abusing children at a Catholic school’s kindergarten, mostly in 2025. More than a dozen families have filed complaints. Prosecutors are investigating, while the local church has opened a preliminary inquiry.

Priest Nicola was seen celebrating Mass at Córdoba’s cathedral in July despite the allegations, angering families of the alleged victims. The Pope is expected to visit the cathedral during his trip. Florencia Navarro and Fernanda Agüero, who accuse Priest Nicola of abusing their daughters, criticised church and school authorities for their handling of the allegations.

“I would like him to provide explanations, since they talk so much about protecting the vulnerable,” Mr. Navarro said of the pope. Ms. Agüero said she hoped the Pope’s message would be backed by “concrete actions” rather than words alone.

Cordoba Archbishop Ángel Rossi invoked the priest’s presumption of innocence when questioned about the case. Priest Nicola has not addressed the allegations, telling journalists only that “the lawyers will take care of that.” His defence team has not commented publicly on the case.

A group of 43 women who allege they were subjected to human trafficking and forced labor at Opus Dei centres in Argentina hope to meet the pope in Buenos Aires.

The allegations implicate senior members of the conservative Catholic organisation, including its global leader, Fernando Ocáriz. Three former Opus Dei vicars in South America and a former regional secretary of its women’s section have been formally accused in the investigation, along with Mariano Fazio, the organisation’s second-highest-ranking official.

Prosecutors have requested that the defendants be summoned for questioning, but the judge has not ordered it. They are also investigating claims that the women were recruited as teenagers under false promises and forced to work 12 to 16 hours a day as domestic servants without pay, under conditions of isolation and strict control, between the 1970s and 2015.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde has announced her resignation effective February 7

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will resign nine months ahead of the end of her term, a move that opens the way for European leaders to choose a successor ahead of France’s presidential election next year.
Ms. Lagarde will leave February 7, the ECB said Thursday (October 29, 2026). Her eight-year term was to end October 31, 2027.
The resignation opens the way for complex political horse trading over her successor and to fill the posts of two other top officials who are leaving next year.

The announcement was not a surprise since there has been speculation that Lagarde would leave early to enable EU leaders to choose a successor while pro-EU French President Emmanuel Macron is still in office. That would guard against the possibility that right-wing presidential candidate Marine Le Pen might win the election and influence the choice.
“That she leaves early is no surprise and does not change the outlook for ECB policies,” said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg bank.
European Council President Antonio Costa said that the selection process “will be initiated today and will proceed without delay.”

The term of another top ECB official — chief economist Philip Lane — is to end May 31, while another member of the ECB’s executive board, Isabel Schnabel, is resigning at year end to move to the International Monetary Fund. European leaders are expected to work out a package deal to apportion the three vacancies among member countries in a complex round of political bargaining.
EU leaders would likely seek to reach agreement on all three posts before a summit meeting on December 17-18, said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg bank.

He said that leading candidates for Lagarde’s job appeared to be former Netherlands central bank head Klaas Knot and Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos, the general manager of the Bank for International Settlements.

“The European Union is trying to guard itself at least somewhat against the risk that right-wing Marine Le Pen may win the French presidential election in April-May 2027,” Mr. Schmieding wrote in an email. “Lagarde’s successor will still be appointed while the staunchly pro-European centrist Emmanuel Macron still resides in the Elysee Palace.”

articles.title: U.K. PM Andy Burnham’s trip to India could take place soon: British Envoy
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keen to visit India and a trip could take place soon, a top U.K. diplomat said on Thursday (October 29, 2026), highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries.

Speaking to PTI, Acting British High Commissioner to India Ben Mellor said Mr. Burnham had conveyed his desire to visit India during a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi after taking office. “I know that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is very keen to come to India," Mr. Mellor said.
"When he and Prime Minister Modi spoke just after he took office as prime minister, he expressed that directly to the prime minister, and I'm sure we'll be able to see that happen soon,” he added.
Mr. Burnham was appointed as prime minister on July 20 this year.
On the India-U.K. economic ties, Mr. Mellor expressed confidence that the two countries would surpass their target of doubling bilateral trade as their economies continue to grow.
The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force 100 days ago. But actually it was signed just over a year ago. Since then we've already seen new deals worth 12 billion pounds, he said.
Comment | An anchor for India-U.K. ties, their economic partnership
“I have every confidence that as the UK and the Indian economies grow, we will surpass the target of doubling trade between our two countries,” Mr. Mellor added.
India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030.

Mr. Mellor also said the U.K. remained strongly welcoming to Indian businesses and investors, noting that Indian investors had been the second-largest source of new investment projects in the country over the past several years.

fullParagraphs: Rescue teams use cranes, dog teams in search for survivors of fatal crash; death toll stands at 68

Rescuers searched desperately through wrecked ⁠carriages on Thursday (October 29, 2026) in the hope of finding more survivors of Spain’s second deadly high-speed train crash this year, which has so far claimed 68 lives.

Emergency workers were seen carrying what appeared ‌to be a body wrapped in a blanket from one of the trains in a rural area in the central province of Toledo as ‌cranes worked through the night to lift parts of the wreckage of Wednesday’s ‌crash.

“Rescue ⁠teams are still working very carefully, because we still cannot say with ⁠certainty that there are no more victims trapped in the twisted wreckage,” Esther Padilla, a spokeswoman for the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, told TVE.
“A canine unit was deployed yesterday. They will go back ​in today to make sure that nobody ‌else remains there,” she added.

Meanwhile, train drivers in Spain went ahead with a previously planned strike to press for more investment in railway safety after what is Europe’s deadliest train accident since a 2013 derailment in Spain’s Santiago de Compostela.

The crash, ‌which followed another fatal accident in January involving the same rail companies ​on the same line, has also upended campaigning for a November 29 snap election, with the leaders of Spain’s two main parties suspending campaign ⁠events.
Spain’s government has declared three days of national mourning for those killed when one high-speed train hit another.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez was ‌due to travel to Toledo on Thursday morning to take part in a meeting to monitor and coordinate the emergency response.
Meanwhile, Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, leader of the centre-right People’s Party (PP), which is currently leading in polls, was due to travel to the town of Urda near the crash site.
The crash has reopened a debate about safety on Spain’s railways, Europe’s longest and until recently a source of pride in the country.

articles.title: Spain train crash: Indian Embassy in Madrid issues helpline after deadly accident
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: After the Spain train crash, the Indian Embassy in Madrid issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403
A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed at least 68 people and injured scores of people on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) , with the death toll expected to rise, authorities said.
Indian Embassy in Madrid has opened an emergency helpline for its nationals after the accident — one of Europe’s deadliest rail disasters this century.

The Indian Embassy in Madrid advised Indian nationals who were travelling on the affected trains, as well as their family members, to contact the mission for immediate assistance. In an advisory posted on its official X account, the Embassy urged people to share details of its emergency helpline with anyone requiring support.
The embassy issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403.

The collision occurred in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday (October 29) morning when a train operated by state-owned Renfe crashed into the rear of a stationary train belonging to private operator Iryo.
ALSO WATCH Deadly train collision in Spain: What we know so far

The second major rail accident to hit Spain in 2026 is likely to renew scrutiny of the country’s railway safety systems, with Transport Minister Óscar Puente referring to an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that preceded the crash. The accident involved a Renfe AVE service and an Iryo train travelling from Madrid to Seville. The impact caused the rear coaches of the Iryo train to derail and plunge down an embankment near kilometre marker 118.

Mr. Puente said preliminary assessments suggested a possible technical failure at the Atocha control centre involving the LZB safety system, though he stressed that the exact cause remained under investigation.

According to the Minister, an automatic train-control system failed over a 69-kilometre stretch of track, resulting in services being halted. However, the control centre later authorised the resumption of traffic despite the disruption.

“The control centre decided to resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable,” Mr. Puente said, adding that the Renfe train travelled around 25 kilometres before colliding with the stationary Iryo service.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab likely drew moisture from Tamil Nadu system, but did not merge
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A lingering low-pressure system near Tamil Nadu may have supplied additional moisture to Arnab, potentially helping sustain its cloud bands and rainfall as it approached the Andhra coast.

Cyclone Arnab has weakened into a depression over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) saying it is “very likely” to weaken further into a well-marked low-pressure area over north-Chhattisgarh and adjoining northwest Odisha by Thursday evening.

The remnant of the very severe cyclonic storm moved nearly northwards at 18 kmph over the past six hours. At 8.30 a.m. on Thursday, it lay about 40 km north-northwest of Jagdalpur in Chhattisgarh, 180 km southwest of Titlagarh in Odisha, 200 km south of Raipur and 310km southwest of Sambalpur.

Arnab had crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam early on October 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 125-135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph. The IMD said the landfall process was completed by 8 a.m. that day.

Weather experts said a lingering low-pressure system near Tamil Nadu may have supplied additional moisture to Arnab, potentially helping sustain its cloud bands and rainfall as it approached the Andhra coast. The interaction also raised the possibility of Arnab becoming more powerful had the two systems combined, though there was no indication that a Fujiwara interaction had occurred.

“Seriously, seeing something like this for the first time! Cyclone Arnab is intensifying like a monster, while the earlier low pressure system that gave Tamil Nadu nearly 10 days of widespread rains is still hanging around as a separate system!” wrote independent weather analyst Ajith Kumar (Chennai Weatherman) on X on October 27.

“ATCF [Automated Tropical Cyclone Forecasting System] has now tagged that system as Invest 90B, previously 99A. Seriously bizarre thing!! It is still lingering around Tamil Nadu’s latitude, but remains far east of the coast to bring significant rains right now. If those both would have combined by now, Arnab could potentially have become an even more powerful system,” Kumar added.
The possibility of the two systems combining highlights how interactions between weather systems can influence a cyclone’s intensity.
In theory, the interaction of two sufficiently developed tropical cyclones can produce a Fujiwara effect, in which they rotate around a common centre and may eventually merge.

However, Arnab was a much stronger system than the lingering low-pressure area near Tamil Nadu. Instead, moisture feeding or partial is more likely to have occurred as they interacted, per weather research .

The Fujiwara effect occurs when two nearby cyclonic systems orbit each other and interact, merging into a single, larger cyclone. The phenomenon is named after Japanese meteorologist Sakuhei Fujiwara, who first described it in the 1920s.

fullParagraphs: The signatories called for a broader effort to strengthen the public health and medical system so that ordinary citizens would not be compelled to abandon government hospitals because of inadequate facilities

“If the public is drifting away from government hospitals and being pushed into the clutches of the corporate healthcare system, it is undeniably because politicians and governments lack genuine sincerity,” said 115 citizens and activists in an open letter to Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha.
The letter accused successive governments of failing to strengthen public healthcare, alleging that the lack of basic amenities in government hospitals is driving patients towards private healthcare.

The letter highlights concerns over drinking water facilities, toilets, sanitation and the maintenance of infrastructure at major government hospitals in Hyderabad, including Osmania General Hospital, Gandhi Hospital, Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Niloufer Hospital and Petlaburj Maternity Hospital.

The signatories — comprising social activists, academics, writers, journalists, teachers and other citizens — questioned whether the government’s promises to improve public healthcare translated into better conditions for patients.

The signatories argued that the challenges confronting government hospitals cannot be viewed solely through the lens of shortages of doctors and other medical personnel. The signatories acknowledged that healthcare workers were already working under considerable pressure, but said the absence of basic amenities was adding to the difficulties faced by patients.
“Government hospitals have experienced doctors, medical staff and research capabilities, but inadequate facilities are undermining the healthcare experience,” they added.

Referring to Osmania, Gandhi, NIMS, Niloufer and Petlaburj hospitals, the signatories questioned why patients should have to endure difficult conditions to access treatment when the institutions were expected to provide essential public healthcare services.

They have identified clean drinking water, functional toilets and proper sanitation as among the most pressing requirements in public hospitals. Questioning the government’s responsibility for maintaining these facilities, the signatories asked whether patients should be held responsible for unhygienic conditions and unpleasant odours in hospital toilets, arguing that the responsibility for maintenance rested with the authorities.
They said patients who could afford private healthcare might choose to seek treatment elsewhere, but those unable to bear the additional expense were left with fewer options.

The signatories also cautioned the government against transferring responsibility for maintaining basic hospital amenities to corporate entities under the banner of public participation as doing so would impose an additional financial burden on patients. They called for the government to take responsibility for improving existing infrastructure and ensuring that essential facilities were properly maintained.

articles.title: Mother’s feeding practices may influence children’s reluctance to try new foods: NIN study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Food neophobia among children can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth

A mother’s knowledge, attitude and feeding practices can significantly influence a child’s willingness to try new foods , which highlights the need for stronger nutrition counselling for caregivers during early childhood, according to a new study by researchers at the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN).

The study, published in the Journal of Nutritional Science , examined food neophobia, a condition in which children are reluctant to try unfamiliar or diverse foods. Such behaviour can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth.

Researchers assessed 150 mother-child pairs from Addagutta in Hyderabad between August and October 2025 focusing on children aged two- seven years and explored how maternal feeding practices were associated with food neophobia and children’s nutritional status.

The findings revealed that nearly 77% of children showed moderate levels of food neophobia, while 11.3% displayed high levels and 12% had low levels. Boys recorded slightly higher food neophobia scores than girls, although the differences were not statistically significant.

The study also found a link between nutritional status and food acceptance. Children suffering from wasting were more likely to exhibit higher food neophobia scores than those with normal nutritional status, suggesting that reluctance to try new foods may be associated with poorer dietary outcomes.

Researchers observed that maternal knowledge, attitudes and practices played an important role. Children whose mothers demonstrated moderate levels of nutrition-related knowledge and positive feeding practices had lower food neophobia scores than those whose mothers had lower scores.

Karthikeyan Ramanujam, Scientist-C at ICMR-NIN and lead author of the study, said the findings underscore the importance of everyday feeding behaviours. He suggested that caregivers should repeatedly offer a variety of foods without pressure, create positive mealtime experiences and respond supportively when children reject unfamiliar foods.

ICMR-NIN Director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings offer an opportunity to strengthen behavioural feeding counselling through existing government programmes such as the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

Researchers cautioned that the study was limited to a single urban low-income community and a relatively small sample size. They noted that, as a cross-sectional study, it identifies associations but cannot establish direct cause-and-effect relationships, as per a press release.

articles.title: Keralam Assembly: Orders issued to procure 2,159 bottles of SMA drug, says Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Replying to a submission, Minister says government is taking several steps through Kerala United Against Rare Diseases scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA

The Kerala government has issued orders for procuring 2,159 bottles of Risdiplam , the first at-home, oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), to ensure continued availability of the medicine, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said.

Replying to a submission by P.K. Firos, MLA, in the Assembly on Thursday, the Minister said the government was taking several steps through the KARE (Kerala United Against Rare Diseases) scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA, a rare, life-threatening genetic disorder that progressively weakens muscles, severely impairing both mobility and respiratory function.
Medicines and related treatment were made available through the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram, he said.

Keralam used to obtain Risdiplam, under its trade name, at a negotiated price of ₹5.5 lakh per bottle. Since October 19, it had been providing a less expensive generic version of the drug manufactured in the country by Natco Pharma. The drug Natsmart cost only around ₹11,000, significantly bringing down treatment costs and making the medicine available to more children.
Besides medicines, the government also provided physiotherapy, respiratory therapy, respiratory devices, rehabilitation, and surgery, the Minister said.
Keralam has been providing Risdiplam free of cost to children under 12 since 2022 through KARE. Steps have been taken to provide all eligible persons the medicine lifelong, he said.

Referring to two children of a couple who had registered with the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital on October 6 and had Type 2 SMA, the Minister said they were eligible for free Risdiplam. Urgent steps were being taken to provide them with treatment the approval of a technical experts committee. Natsmart was being provided to them. Medicines and treatment would be provided to the couple’s third child through KARE on completion of check-up, he added.

The government would also consider devising more comprehensive programmes in association with the Kerala Social Security Mission to provide treatment and financial and psychological support to the affected children and their families. The government, the Minister said, was committed to ensuring that treatment was not disrupted, medicines were available continuously, and the financial burden on families was reduced.

Replying to a submission, Minister says government is taking several steps through Kerala United Against Rare Diseases scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA

The Kerala government has issued orders for procuring 2,159 bottles of Risdiplam , the first at-home, oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), to ensure continued availability of the medicine, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said.

Replying to a submission by P.K. Firos, MLA, in the Assembly on Thursday, the Minister said the government was taking several steps through the KARE (Kerala United Against Rare Diseases) scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA, a rare, life-threatening genetic disorder that progressively weakens muscles, severely impairing both mobility and respiratory function.

Medicines and related treatment were made available through the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram, he said.

Keralam used to obtain Risdiplam, under its trade name, at a negotiated price of ₹5.5 lakh per bottle. Since October 19, it had been providing a less expensive generic version of the drug manufactured in the country by Natco Pharma. The drug Natsmart cost only around ₹11,000, significantly bringing down treatment costs and making the medicine available to more children.

Besides medicines, the government also provided physiotherapy, respiratory therapy, respiratory devices, rehabilitation, and surgery, the Minister said.

Keralam has been providing Risdiplam free of cost to children under 12 since 2022 through KARE. Steps have been taken to provide all eligible persons the medicine lifelong, he said.

Referring to two children of a couple who had registered with the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital on October 6 and had Type 2 SMA, the Minister said they were eligible for free Risdiplam. Urgent steps were being taken to provide them with treatment the approval of a technical experts committee. Natsmart was being provided to them. Medicines and treatment would be provided to the couple’s third child through KARE on completion of check-up, he added.

The government would also consider devising more comprehensive programmes in association with the Kerala Social Security Mission to provide treatment and financial and psychological support to the affected children and their families. The government, the Minister said, was committed to ensuring that treatment was not disrupted, medicines were available continuously, and the financial burden on families was reduced.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The government would also consider devising more comprehensive programmes in association with the Kerala Social Security Mission to provide treatment and financial and psychological support to the affected children and their families. articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: India votes in favour of UNGA resolution calling for end to US embargo on Cuba
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on October 28, with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining

India voted in favour of a UN General Assembly resolution calling for an end to the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the U.S. against Cuba, reiterating that the restrictions should be lifted to help the Caribbean nation pursue its development aspirations.
The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining.

Delivering India's statement, Counsellor at India's Permanent Mission to the UN Soumya Nair said the General Assembly has repeatedly called for an end to the embargo and rejected laws and regulations with extraterritorial effects that adversely affect the sovereignty of other states and the progress and prosperity of their peoples.

"India reiterates the Assembly's call to all states to refrain from promulgating and applying, and to repeal and invalidate, such laws and measures in conformity with their obligations under the Charter of the United Nations and international law," she said.
Ms. Nair said India's commitment to multilateralism is rooted in the belief that international challenges are best addressed through dialogue and diplomacy, in accordance with the UN Charter.

"It is in this spirit that India hopes that the embargo will be lifted at the earliest to help create an environment that would enable the people of Cuba to participate more fully in international cooperation and pursue their legitimate development aspirations,” she said.
Citing a report by the UN Secretary-General, Ms. Nair highlighted the impact of the restrictions on Cuba's economy and essential services.
Cuba's health system faces shortages of over 60% of essential medicines, while food production has declined by more than 50% in the past five years, she said.

“The restrictions on fuel exports to Cuba have also aggravated the country's ongoing energy crisis. The shortages have disrupted essential services, including healthcare, education, water supplies, food distribution, and transportation,” Ms. Nair said.

The conflict between America and Cuba stems from a decades-old political, economic, and ideological divide that began when Fidel Castro overthrew a U.S.-backed government in 1959 and aligned the island with the Soviet Union.
